sentences.zh: 劉毅

translations.literal: Liu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 劉毅，字仲雄，東萊掖人。

translations.literal: Liu Yi, courtesy name Zhongxiong, was a native of Ye in Donglai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, styled Zhongxiong, came from Ye in Donglai.

sentences.zh: 漢城陽景王章之後。

translations.literal: He was descended from Prince Jing of Chengyang, Liu Zhang, of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: He traced his ancestry to Prince Jing of Chengyang, Liu Zhang, under the Han.

sentences.zh: 父喈，丞相屬。

translations.literal: His father Jie was an aide on the Chancellor's staff.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Liu Gu, served as an aide to the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 毅幼有孝行，少厲清節，然好臧否人物，王公貴人望風憚之。

translations.literal: Yi from childhood had conduct of filial piety; in youth he hardened pure integrity, yet he loved to praise or blame others, and princes and nobles feared him at the mere rumor.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was dutiful as a boy and austere in morals, but he freely praised and censured people, and even kings and grandees learned to dread him.

sentences.zh: 僑居平陽，太守杜恕請為功曹，沙汰郡吏百餘人，三魏稱焉。

translations.literal: Sojourning in Pingyang, Prefect Du Shu asked him to be merit assessor; he winnowed out over a hundred clerks of the commandery, and the Three Wei praised this.
translations.idiomatic: While residing in Pingyang as a guest, he became Du Shu's merit assessor, removed more than a hundred county officers, and men across the Three Wei applauded him.

sentences.zh: 為之語曰：「但聞劉功曹，不聞杜府君。

translations.literal: They made a saying of it: "One hears only of Merit Assessor Liu, not of Prefect Du."
translations.idiomatic: People rhymed: "You hear about Registrar Liu, never about Governor Du."

sentences.zh: 」魏末，本郡察孝廉，辟司隸都官從事，京邑肅然。

translations.literal: " At the end of Wei his home commandery nominated him Filial and Incorrupt; he was summoned as attendant clerk for capital crimes under the Metropolitan Governor, and the capital became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wei his county recommended him as filial and honest; he became a clerk under the metropolitan governor for capital cases, and order settled over the capital.

sentences.zh: 毅將彈河南尹，司隸不許，曰：「攫獸之犬，鼷鼠蹈其背。

translations.literal: Yi was about to impeach the Governor of Henan; the Metropolitan Governor did not permit it, saying, "The dog that seizes beasts—a shrew-mouse treads on its back."
translations.idiomatic: When Yi moved to impeach the governor of Henan, the metropolitan governor vetoed him: "The hound that takes prey still has a mouse scamper across its back."

sentences.zh: 」毅曰：「既能攫獸，又能殺鼠，何損於犬！

translations.literal: " Yi said, "If it can seize beasts, it can also kill rats—what harm to the dog!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi retorted, "If it can bring down game, it can kill vermin—what insult is that to the hound?"

sentences.zh: 」投傳而去。

translations.literal: " He cast aside his credentials and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He slammed down his commission and walked off.

sentences.zh: 同郡王基薦毅於公府，曰：「毅方正亮直，介然不群，言不苟合，行不苟容。

translations.literal: Wang Ji of the same commandery recommended Yi to the public bureau, saying, "Yi is upright, bright, and straight; he stands apart and does not flock with others; in speech he does not lightly agree, in conduct he does not lightly accommodate."
translations.idiomatic: His fellow townsman Wang Ji urged him on the great council: "Yi is square, candid, and blunt—set apart from factions; he will not trim his words or manners to please."

sentences.zh: 往日僑仕平陽，為郡股肱，正色立朝，舉綱引墨，朱紫有分，《鄭》、《衛》不雜，孝弟著于邦族，忠貞效于三魏。

translations.literal: In former days he sojourned and served in Pingyang as the commandery's thigh and arm; with stern dignity he stood in court, raising the guideline and applying the ink-line; crimson and purple had their divisions; the airs of Zheng and Wei did not mix; filial piety and fraternal duty showed in his clan; loyalty and steadfastness had effect across the Three Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, posted in Pingyang, he was the prefect's mainstay; he faced court with a straight spine, pulled guideline and plumb line so ranks stayed sorted and coarse music never crept in—filial duty shone in his kin, loyalty across the Three Wei.

sentences.zh: 昔孫陽取騏驥于吳阪，秦穆拔百里於商旅。

translations.literal: Of old Sun Yang took swift horses on the slopes of Wu; Duke Mu of Qin raised Baili Xi from traveling merchants.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yang once picked fleet horses on the Wu hills; Duke Mu of Qin lifted Baili Xi straight out of the caravan trade.

sentences.zh: 毅未遇知己，無所自呈。

translations.literal: Yi has not yet encountered one who knows him and has nowhere to display himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yi still lacks a patron who recognizes him and has nowhere to show what he can do.

sentences.zh: 前已口白，謹復申請。

translations.literal: Previously I have spoken orally; I respectfully submit the request again.
translations.idiomatic: I reported this earlier in person; I now renew the request in writing.

sentences.zh: 」太常鄭袤舉博士，文帝辟為相國掾，辭疾，積年不就。

translations.literal: " The Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Mao nominated him as erudite; Emperor Wen summoned him as aide to the minister of state, but citing illness he declined for years without taking office.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zheng Mao nominated him as a doctorate holder; Emperor Wen called him to the chancellor's staff, yet he pleaded sickness and stayed away for years.

sentences.zh: 時人謂毅忠於魏氏，而帝怒其顧望，將加重辟。

translations.literal: People of the time said Yi was loyal to the house of Wei, but the Emperor was angry at his hesitation and was going to impose the heavy punishment of execution.
translations.idiomatic: Observers credited Yi with loyalty to Wei; the emperor read his stalling as defiance and meant to execute him.

sentences.zh: 毅懼，應命，轉主薄。

translations.literal: Yi feared, answered the summons, and was transferred to chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Yi obeyed and was reassigned as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，為尚書郎、駙馬都尉，遷散騎常侍、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, Yi became Gentleman of the Palace and Commandant of Cavalry for the Princess's Household, then was promoted to regular attendant at casual riding and libationer of the National Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin founder took the throne, Yi served as palace gentleman and commandant of consort cavalry, then rose to imperial attendant and rector of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 帝以毅忠蹇正直，使掌諫官。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Yi was loyal, blunt, and upright, made him oversee remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put Yi—steadfast and blunt—in charge of the remonstrance corps.

sentences.zh: 轉城門校尉，遷太僕，拜尚書，坐事免官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to colonel of the City Gates, promoted to grand coachman, appointed minister of state affairs, then dismissed from office for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He rotated through colonel of the gates and minister of the imperial stud, became minister of state affairs, then lost his post over an incident.

sentences.zh: 咸寧初，復為散騎常侍、博士祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianning he again became regular attendant at casual riding and libationer of erudites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning he returned as attendant-in-ordinary and libationer over the classicists.

sentences.zh: 轉司隸校尉，糾正豪右，京師肅然。

translations.literal: He was transferred to metropolitan governor; he corrected powerful families on the right, and the capital became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: As metropolitan governor he reined in great houses until the capital fell quiet.

sentences.zh: 司部守令望風投印綬者甚眾，時人以毅方之諸葛豐、蓋寬饒。

translations.literal: Very many prefects and magistrates of the metropolitan circuit cast aside their seals at the rumor of him; men of the time compared Yi to Zhuge Feng and Gai Kuangrao.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects up and down the capital circuit surrendered their seals at his approach; contemporaries likened him to Zhuge Feng and Gai Kuangrao.

sentences.zh: 皇太子朝，鼓吹將入東掖門，毅以為不敬，止之於門外，奏劾保傅以下。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent attended court, the military musicians were about to enter the eastern inner gate; Yi deemed it disrespectful, stopped them outside the gate, and memorialized to impeach all from the tutors downward.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince came to court, the military band tried to pass the eastern inner gate; Yi judged it a breach of ritual, blocked them outside, and impeached everyone from the tutors on down.

sentences.zh: 詔赦之，然後得入。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned them; afterward they were allowed to enter.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted amnesty; only then could they enter.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗南郊，禮畢，喟然問毅曰：「卿以朕方漢何帝也？

translations.literal: Once when the Emperor had sacrificed at the southern suburb and the rites were finished, he sighed and asked Yi, "You liken Us to which emperor of the Han?"
translations.idiomatic: After a southern-suburb sacrifice the emperor sighed and asked Yi, "Whom among the Han emperors do you compare Us to?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「可方桓、靈。

translations.literal: " He replied, "One may compare to Huan and Ling."
translations.idiomatic: Yi answered, "About on a level with Emperors Huan and Ling."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「吾雖德不及古人，猶克己為政。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "Though Our virtue does not reach the ancients, still We restrain Ourselves in governing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Even if Our virtue falls short of antiquity, We still discipline Ourselves in government."

sentences.zh: 又平吳會，混一天下。

translations.literal: Moreover We have pacified Wu and the Hui region and mixed into one the realm.
translations.idiomatic: We have also crushed Wu, brought the southeast to heel, and united the realm.

sentences.zh: 方之桓、靈，其已甚乎！

translations.literal: Compared with Huan and Ling, would it not already be excessive!
translations.idiomatic: Stack us beside Huan and Ling—surely that is going too far!

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「桓、靈賣官，錢入官庫；

translations.literal: " He replied, "Huan and Ling sold offices; the money entered the official treasury;"
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied, "Under Huan and Ling, office-selling filled the state treasury;"

sentences.zh: 陛下賣官，錢入私門。

translations.literal: when Your Majesty sells offices, the money enters private households.
translations.idiomatic: when Your Majesty sells offices, the silver lines private pockets.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，殆不如也。

translations.literal: Judged by this say, perhaps not equal.
translations.idiomatic: On that score, Your Majesty may even fall short of them.

sentences.zh: 」帝大笑曰：「桓靈之世，不聞此言。

translations.literal: " The Emperor laughed greatly and said, "In the age of Huan and Ling one did not hear these words."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor roared with laughter. "In Huan and Ling's day no one dared say such a thing."

sentences.zh: 今有直臣，故不同也。

translations.literal: Now there is a straight minister; therefore it is not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Now We have a minister who speaks plain truth—that is the difference.

sentences.zh: 」散騎常侍鄒湛進曰：「世談以陛下比漢文帝，人心猶不多同。

translations.literal: " Regular attendant at casual riding Zou Zhen stepped forward and said, "Worldly talk compares Your Majesty to Emperor Wen of Han, yet people's hearts still are not much agreed."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Zou Zhen added, "Common opinion ranks Your Majesty with Emperor Wen of Han, yet many hearts still withhold full assent."

sentences.zh: 昔馮唐答文帝，雲不能用頗牧而文帝怒，今劉毅言犯順而陛下歡。

translations.literal: Of old Feng Tang answered Emperor Wen; because he said Wen could not employ Po and Mu, Emperor Wen was angry; now Liu Yi speaks offending compliance yet Your Majesty rejoices.
translations.idiomatic: Once Feng Tang told Emperor Wen he could not use Lian Po and Li Mu, and Wen flared with rage; today Liu Yi speaks against the grain and Your Majesty beams."

sentences.zh: 然以此相校，聖德乃過之矣。

translations.literal: Yet by this contrast, sagely virtue then surpasses his.
translations.idiomatic: Weighed that way, Your sagely virtue outshines Wen's."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「我平天下而不封禪，焚雉頭裘，行布衣禮，卿初無言。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "We pacified the realm yet did not perform Feng and Shan; We burned the pheasant-head fur robe and observed ceremonies in plain cloth—yet you at first said nothing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "We conquered the realm yet declined the Feng and Shan sacrifices, burned the pheasant-feather cloak, and wore common cloth at court—and you kept silent."

sentences.zh: 今于小事，何見褒之甚？

translations.literal: Now on a small matter, why is the praise seen so great?
translations.idiomatic: Why lavish such praise on so slight a point?

sentences.zh: 」湛曰：「臣聞猛獸在田，荷戈而出，凡人能之。

translations.literal: " Zhen said, "Your servant has heard that when a fierce beast is in the field, shouldering a spear and going out—ordinary men can do it."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen replied, "They say when a beast ranges the field, any man can grab a spear and face it.

sentences.zh: 蜂蠆作於懷袖，勇夫為之驚駭，出於意外故也。

translations.literal: When hornets breed in sleeve and bosom, brave men are alarmed by it—because it comes from beyond expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Let hornets nest in your sleeve and even the bravest flinch—because danger arrives unlooked-for.

sentences.zh: 夫君臣有自然之尊卑，言語有自然之逆順。

translations.literal: Between lord and minister there is natural honor and humility; in speech there is natural opposition and compliance.
translations.idiomatic: Lord and subject observe a natural order of rank; words follow a natural course of deference or bluntness.

sentences.zh: 向劉毅始言，臣等莫不變色。

translations.literal: When Liu Yi first spoke, we ministers none did not change color.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi first spoke, every one of us went pale.

sentences.zh: 陛下發不世之詔，出思慮之表，臣之喜慶，不亦宜乎！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty issued an edict not of this age, venturing beyond deliberation—your servant's joy and celebration, is it not fitting!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty answered with words rare in any reign, beyond ordinary counsel—how could we not rejoice?

sentences.zh: 在職六年，遷尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Having been in office six years, he was promoted to vice director of the left of the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After six years in post he became vice director of the left at the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時龍見武庫井中，帝親觀之，有喜色。

translations.literal: At that time a dragon appeared in a well of the armory; the Emperor viewed it in person and had a pleased expression.
translations.idiomatic: A dragon appeared in an armory well; the emperor went to see it himself and looked delighted.

sentences.zh: 百官將賀，毅獨表曰：「昔龍降鄭時門之外，子產不賀。

translations.literal: When the hundred officials were about to congratulate, Yi alone submitted a memorial saying: "Of old when a dragon descended outside the gate of Shi in Zheng, Zichan did not congratulate."
translations.idiomatic: As the court prepared congratulations, Yi alone memorialized: "Long ago a dragon alighted outside Zheng's Gate of Shi; Zichan refused to celebrate."

sentences.zh: 龍降夏庭，沫流不禁，卜藏其漦，至周幽王，禍釁乃發。

translations.literal: A dragon descended in the Xia court; foam flowed unstoppable; they divined and hid its saliva; down to King You of Zhou the calamity and breach then broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Another dragon settled in the Xia hall—froth ran unchecked; diviners hid its spittle, yet disaster erupted under King You of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱'潛龍勿用，陽在下也。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes calls it 'the submerged dragon—do not employ; the yang line lies below.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes reads: 'Hidden dragon, do not act'—the yang force still lies low.

sentences.zh: '證據舊典，無賀龍之禮。

translations.literal: ' Examining evidence in old canons, there is no rite for congratulating dragons.
translations.idiomatic: The canon offers no precedent for toasting a dragon as auspicious.

sentences.zh: 」詔報曰：「正德未修，誠未有以膺受嘉祥。

translations.literal: " An edict replied: "Proper virtue is not yet cultivated; truly there is not yet title to receive auspicious signs."
translations.idiomatic: The court answered: "Our moral cultivation falls short; We are hardly worthy of such omens."

sentences.zh: 省來示，以為瞿然。

translations.literal: Examining what you submitted, We thereby became startled.
translations.idiomatic: Your memorial gave Us pause.

sentences.zh: 賀慶之事，宜詳依典義，動靜數示。

translations.literal: Matters of congratulation and celebration ought in detail follow canonical meaning; movements and stillness frequently show.
translations.idiomatic: Hold any celebration strictly to classical precedent, and keep Us informed as circumstances shift.

sentences.zh: 」尚書郎劉漢等議，以為：「龍體既蒼，雜以素文，意者大晉之行，戢武興文之應也。

translations.literal: " Ministers Lang Liu Han and others debated and held: "The dragon's body being dark blue mixed with plain markings, presumably this intends the conduct of Great Jin—the correspondence of laying aside arms and raising culture."
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Liu Han and colleagues argued: "The beast shows azure hide streaked with white—surely an omen that Great Jin will sheath swords and lift letters.

sentences.zh: 而毅乃引衰世妖異，以疑今之吉祥。

translations.literal: Yet Yi then cites omens of a declining age and casts doubt on today's auspiciousness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yi dredges up freak signs from fallen dynasties to discredit today's blessing.

sentences.zh: 又以龍在井為潛，皆失其意。

translations.literal: Moreover taking the dragon in the well as submerged—both lose its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Calling a well dragon 'hidden' also misses the point entirely.

sentences.zh: 潛之為言，隱而不見。

translations.literal: As for 'submerged,' in what it says—it hides and is not seen.
translations.idiomatic: "Hidden" means concealed from sight—nothing like this blazing beast.

sentences.zh: 今龍彩質明煥，示人以物，非潛之謂也。

translations.literal: Now the dragon's colors and substance shine bright, showing men a thing—it is not what is called 'submerged.'
translations.idiomatic: This creature gleams in full view—hardly a 'hidden' dragon.

sentences.zh: 毅應推處。

translations.literal: Yi ought to be referred for disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Refer Liu Yi for discipline.

sentences.zh: 」詔不聽。

translations.literal: " The edict did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ignored the motion.

sentences.zh: 後陰氣解而復合，毅上言：「必有阿黨之臣，奸以事君者，當誅而不誅故也。

translations.literal: Later yin-qi dissolved and then recombined; Yi submitted: "There must be ministers of clique and faction, and those who use deceit to serve the ruler—because those who ought to be executed have not been executed."
translations.idiomatic: When yin mists parted and closed again, Yi wrote: "Some toadying clique is at work—villains who should die but go unpunished."

sentences.zh: 毅以魏立九品，權時之制，未見得人，而有八損，乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: Yi held that Wei's establishing the nine ranks was a system for the expedient moment; he had not seen gaining of men, yet there were eight harms—thereupon he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Judging Wei's nine-grade scheme an emergency expedient that rewarded mediocrity yet brought eight kinds of harm, Yi memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣聞：立政者，以官才為本，官才有三難，而興替之所由也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: those who establish government take official talent as root; official talent has three difficulties, and these are the grounds by which rise and decline occur.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has learned that sound rule rests on placing talent, yet talent presents three stubborn puzzles—the hinge on which dynasties flourish or fail.

sentences.zh: 人物難知，一也；

translations.literal: Men are hard to know—first;
translations.idiomatic: First, knowing men is hard;

sentences.zh: 愛憎難防，二也；

translations.literal: Love and hate are hard to guard against—second;
translations.idiomatic: second, partisan liking and loathing slip past every guard;

sentences.zh: 情偽難明，三也。

translations.literal: True feeling and falsehood are hard to clarify—third.
translations.idiomatic: third, sincerity and pretense hide behind the same smile.

sentences.zh: 今立中正，定九品，高下任意，榮辱在手。

translations.literal: Now establishing the impartial judges and fixing the nine ranks, high and low follow whim; glory and shame rest in the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet installing regional graders and fixing nine ranks leaves promotion and ruin to private whim.

sentences.zh: 操人主之威福，奪天朝之權勢。

translations.literal: They wield the awesome fortune of the lord of men and seize the power and momentum of the celestial court.
translations.idiomatic: Graders wield imperial favor and siphon the central government's authority.

sentences.zh: 愛憎決於心，情偽由於己。

translations.literal: Love and hate are decided in the heart; true feeling and falsehood come from oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Private likes settle rank; sincerity or sham rests with them alone.

sentences.zh: 公無考校之負，私無告訐之忌。

translations.literal: Public office bears no burden of examination and verification; private quarters lack fear of accusation and expose.
translations.idiomatic: The crown cannot audit them; informers dare not touch them.

sentences.zh: 用心百態，求者萬端。

translations.literal: Hearts employ a hundred forms; seekers have myriad beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: Schemes multiply by the hundred; petitioners swarm by the thousand.

sentences.zh: 廉讓之風滅，苟且之欲成。

translations.literal: The wind of integrity and yielding perishes; desires of expediency succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Integrity withers while cynical ambition thrives.

sentences.zh: 天下訩訩，但爭品位，不聞推讓，竊為聖朝恥之。

translations.literal: Under Heaven clamorous—only striving over rank and grade; none hears of yielding and deferring; your servant privately feels shame for the sagely court.
translations.idiomatic: The realm buzzes with quarrels over grades alone—no one yields place—and Your servant cringes for this enlightened dynasty.

sentences.zh: 夫名狀以當才為清，品輩以得實為平，安危之要，不可不明。

translations.literal: Now descriptive labels consider matching talent as clarity; grade ranks consider obtaining truth as fairness—the essentials of safety and danger cannot fail to be clarified.
translations.idiomatic: Profiles must pair talent to rank clarity; bands must pair facts to fairness—the hinge of stability hangs here.

sentences.zh: 清平者，政化之美也；

translations.literal: Clarity and fairness are the beauty of governing transformation;
translations.idiomatic: Fair sorting crowns good rule;

sentences.zh: 枉濫者，亂敗之惡也，不可不察。

translations.literal: twisting and overflow are the evil of disorder and defeat; they cannot fail to be examined.
translations.idiomatic: twisted favoritism foretells chaos and demands scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 然人才異能，備體者釁。

translations.literal: Yet men's talents differ in kind; few are complete in every capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet gifts differ, and few mortals excel in every faculty at once.

sentences.zh: 器有大小，達有早晚。

translations.literal: Vessels have large and small; attainment has early and late.
translations.idiomatic: Some vessels hold much, some little; some ripen early, some late.

sentences.zh: 前鄙後修，宜受日新之報；

translations.literal: Formerly base, later cultivated—ought to receive reward of daily renewal;
translations.idiomatic: Men once coarse who later refine deserve recognition for renewed virtue;

sentences.zh: 抱正違時，宜有質直之稱；

translations.literal: Embracing rectitude but opposing the times—ought to have reputation of substance and straightness;
translations.idiomatic: those upright yet out of step with fashion merit praise as bluntly honest;

sentences.zh: 度遠闕小，宜得殊俗之狀；

translations.literal: Measuring far but lacking in small matters—ought to obtain appearance of extraordinary manner;
translations.idiomatic: those grand in vision though rough in detail should earn marks as unconventional talents;

sentences.zh: 任直不飾，宜得清實之譽；

translations.literal: Trusting straightness without adornment—ought to obtain praise of clarity and substance;
translations.idiomatic: those candid without polish deserve reputations for lucid substance;

sentences.zh: 行寡才優，宜獲器任之用。

translations.literal: Conduct narrow but talent superior—ought to obtain employment of instrumental duty.
translations.idiomatic: those spare in conduct yet rich in skill fit specialized appointments.

sentences.zh: 是以三仁殊途而同歸，四子異行而均義。

translations.literal: Therefore the three benevolent men differed in road yet returned alike; the four masters differed in conduct yet matched in righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Three Worthies walked divergent roads toward one humanity; the Four Masters matched one another in integrity despite unlike paths.

sentences.zh: 陳平、韓信笑侮於邑裏，而收功於帝王；

translations.literal: Chen Ping and Han Xin were laughed at and insulted in village and hamlet, yet gathered merit under emperors and kings;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ping and Han Xin were mocked in their lanes yet crowned service under heaven;

sentences.zh: 屈原、伍胥不容於人主，而顯名於竹帛，是篤論之所明也。

translations.literal: Qu Yuan and Wu Xu were not tolerated by lords of men, yet displayed name on bamboo and silk—this is what thorough discourse makes clear.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yuan and Wu Zixu won no favor from kings yet live on in ink—the histories prove as much.

sentences.zh: 今之中正，不精才實，務依黨利，不均稱尺，備隨愛憎。

translations.literal: Now the impartial judges do not refine talent and substance; they strive to rely on faction and profit; they do not evenly balance the measuring rod; they wholly follow love and hate.
translations.idiomatic: Today's graders ignore real merit, chase factional gain, skew every yardstick, and follow private spite.

sentences.zh: 所欲與者，獲虛以成譽；

translations.literal: Those whom they desire to favor obtain emptiness and thereby complete reputation;
translations.idiomatic: Favorites win hollow praise;

sentences.zh: 所欲下者，吹毛以求疵。

translations.literal: those whom they desire to demote—blowing fur to seek flaws.
translations.idiomatic: targets they dislike endure hair-splitting fault-finding.

sentences.zh: 高下逐強弱，是非由愛憎。

translations.literal: High and low follow strong and weak; right and wrong come from love and hate.
translations.idiomatic: Rank tracks brute strength; verdicts track private spite.

sentences.zh: 隨世興衰，不顧才實，衰則削下，興則扶上，一人之身，旬日異狀。

translations.literal: Following the world's rise and decline, they disregard talent and substance; declining then they cut down; rising then they prop up—in one man's body, within ten days divergent descriptions.
translations.idiomatic: They surf fashion's tides, ignoring substance—demoting the fallen, puffing the ascendant—so one man's file changes shape within days.

sentences.zh: 或以貨賂自通，或以計協登進，附托者必達，守道者困悴。

translations.literal: Some by goods and bribes open passage for themselves; some by schemes and agreements ascend; those who attach and rely surely succeed; those who guard the Way are distressed and worn.
translations.idiomatic: Some buy promotion, some scheme their way up—clients of power rise while principled men wither.

sentences.zh: 無報於身，必見割奪。

translations.literal: If there is no response to oneself, one is sure to see cutting and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: Without patrons, expect ranks stripped away.

sentences.zh: 有私於己，必得其欲。

translations.literal: If there is private favor toward oneself, one surely obtains one's desire.
translations.idiomatic: Win the grader's favor and every wish is granted.

sentences.zh: 是以上品無寒門，下品無勢族。

translations.literal: Therefore in the upper ranks there are no cold gates; in the lower ranks there are no powerful clans.
translations.idiomatic: Hence top grades never reach humble houses; bottom grades never touch great lineages.

sentences.zh: 暨時有之，皆曲有故。

translations.literal: When such occasionally exist, all have crooked reasons.
translations.idiomatic: Any exception stems from back-room dealing.

sentences.zh: 慢主罔時，實為亂源。

translations.literal: Disrespecting the lord and deceiving the times—truly this is the source of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Slighting the throne and mocking the age—this is how chaos begins.

sentences.zh: 損政之道一也。

translations.literal: This is the first way it harms governance.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first way the system undermines good rule.

sentences.zh: 置州都者，取州里清議，咸所歸服，將以鎮異同，一言議。

translations.literal: Those who establish the provincial rectifier take pure opinion of the district, what all submit to, intending thereby to settle divergences and unify discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial graders were meant to voice local consensus and settle disputes—one standard for the circuit.

sentences.zh: 不謂一人之身，了一州之才，一人不審便坐之。

translations.literal: It does not mean one man's person exhausts one province's talent—one misjudgment and they sit in judgment.
translations.idiomatic: That never meant one man could judge every talent in a province or condemn another on a single slip.

sentences.zh: 若然，自仲尼以上，至於庖犧，莫不有失，則皆不堪，何獨責于中人者哉！

translations.literal: If so, from Confucius upward to Fuxi none would be without fault—then all would be unfit—why blame only middling men!
translations.idiomatic: If that were the standard, even Confucius and Fuxi would fail—why single out ordinary officers?

sentences.zh: 若殊不修，自可更選。

translations.literal: If someone is utterly incorrigible, one may simply choose another.
translations.idiomatic: When a man proves utterly unfit, replace him.

sentences.zh: 今重其任而輕其人，所立品格，還訪刁攸。

translations.literal: Now they weight the office and slight the man; the rank established still consults Diao You.
translations.idiomatic: Today the title weighs heavy while the holder counts for little—the grades still circle back to Diao You.

sentences.zh: 攸非州里之所歸，非職分之所置。

translations.literal: You is not what the district submits to, nor what the duty assigns.
translations.idiomatic: You commands neither local trust nor an office built for this task.

sentences.zh: 今訪之，歸正於所不服，決事於所不職，以長讒構之源，以生乖爭之兆，似非立都之本旨，理俗之深防也。

translations.literal: Now consulting him—submitting to rectification where men do not submit, deciding matters outside his competence—lengthens the spring of slander, breeds the omen of quarrel—this seems not the root purpose of establishing the rectifier, nor the deep dyke for ordering custom.
translations.idiomatic: Consulting him forces acceptance where none exists and rulings beyond his brief—it feeds slander and quarrels, betraying why the office was created or how to steady popular conduct.

sentences.zh: 主者既善刁攸，攸之所下而復選以二千石，已有數人。

translations.literal: The chief already favors Diao You; those whom You demoted have again been selected as two-thousand-bushel officials—already several men.
translations.idiomatic: The chief favors You; several men You downgraded have already been picked for governor posts.

sentences.zh: 劉良上攸之所下，石公罪攸之所行，駁違之論橫於州里，嫌讎之隙結于大臣。

translations.literal: Liu Liang appealed what You had demoted; Minister Shi faulted what You had done; conflicting judgments crisscrossed the province; rifts of hatred formed among great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang appealed You's demotions; Minister Shi condemned You's actions—cross-purposes shattered the province and embittered high ministers.

sentences.zh: 夫桑妾之訟，禍及吳、楚；

translations.literal: As for the mulberry-girls' lawsuit—calamity reached Wu and Chu;
translations.idiomatic: A quarrel over mulberry girls embroiled Wu and Chu;

sentences.zh: 鬥雞之變，難興魯邦。

translations.literal: the cockfight affair—disaster arose in the state of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: a cockfight nearly ruined Lu.

sentences.zh: 況乃人倫交爭而部黨興，刑獄滋生而禍根結。

translations.literal: How much more when human relations clash and factions rise, lawsuits multiply and the roots of disaster knot.
translations.idiomatic: How much worse when kin feud, factions sprout, lawsuits breed, and calamity takes root.

sentences.zh: 損政之道二也。

translations.literal: This is the second way it harms governance.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second wound to good rule.

sentences.zh: 本立格之體，將謂人倫有序，若貫魚成次也。

translations.literal: Originally the framework of establishing ranks was intended to mean human relations had order, like strung fish forming sequence.
translations.idiomatic: The ranking system was meant to order society like fish strung on a cord.

sentences.zh: 為九品者，取下者為格，謂才德有優劣，倫輩有首尾。

translations.literal: Those who make the nine ranks take the lower evaluation as the rule, saying talent and virtue have better and worse, and cohorts have head and tail.
translations.idiomatic: Nine-grade assessments treat the lower verdict as standard—talent and virtue differ, and cohorts stack high to low.

sentences.zh: 今之中正，務自遠者，則抑割一國，使無上人；

translations.literal: Now the impartial judges, striving for those from afar, then suppress and cut a whole state so it has no superior men;
translations.idiomatic: Today's graders, chasing outsiders, will suppress an entire region until no local talent ranks high;

sentences.zh: 穢劣下比，則拔舉非次，並容其身。

translations.literal: base and vile men compared below—then they promote out of order and together tolerate their persons.
translations.idiomatic: pair base men down the list and they promote cronies out of turn while sheltering them.

sentences.zh: 公以為格，坐成其私。

translations.literal: Public office they treat as rule—sitting, they complete their private ends.
translations.idiomatic: They wield public rank as cover and finish their private deals.

sentences.zh: 君子無大小之怨，官政無繩奸之防。

translations.literal: Good men harbor no small or great resentment; official governance has no cord against wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Honest men swallow every slight; the bench offers no rope on villainy.

sentences.zh: 使得上欺明主，下亂人倫。

translations.literal: This causes above to deceive the enlightened lord, below to disorder human relations.
translations.idiomatic: So they hoodwink the throne above and unravel society below.

sentences.zh: 乃使優劣易地，首尾倒錯。

translations.literal: Thereby they make better and worse exchange places, head and tail inverted.
translations.idiomatic: Merit and mediocrity swap places; the order turns upside down.

sentences.zh: 推貴異之器，使在凡品之下，負戴不肖，越在成人之首。

translations.literal: They push vessels of rare excellence so they sit below common grades; they bear and carry the unworthy, crossing them above finished men.
translations.idiomatic: Rare talent is ranked below mediocrity; hopeless dolts vault above men of substance.

sentences.zh: 損政之道三也。

translations.literal: This is the third way it harms governance.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third blow to good rule.

sentences.zh: 陛下踐阼，開天地之德，弘不諱之詔，納忠直之言，以覽天下之情，太平之基，不世之法也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty mounted the throne, opened Heaven-and-Earth virtue, expanded the edict of no taboo, admitted loyal straight speech, thereby to survey the feelings of all under Heaven—the foundation of great peace, a law not of one age.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's accession spread cosmic generosity, welcomed blunt counsel, and opened every grievance—the cornerstone of lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 然嘗罰，自王公以至於庶人，無不加法。

translations.literal: Yet in rewards and punishments, from kings and dukes down to commoners, none fail to have law applied.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments reach from princes to commoners—no one escapes the law.

sentences.zh: 置中正，委以一國之重，無嘗罰之防。

translations.literal: Yet establishing the impartial judge, entrusting him with the weight of a state—there is no guard of rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Yet we hand a state's fate to a regional grader with no reward or penalty to restrain him.

sentences.zh: 人心多故，清平者寡，故怨訟者眾。

translations.literal: Men's hearts have many causes; the clear and fair are few; therefore the resentful and litigious are many.
translations.idiomatic: Hearts breed endless excuses; few stay impartial, so lawsuits swarm.

sentences.zh: 聽之則告訐無已，禁絕則侵枉無極，與其理訟之煩，猶愈侵枉之害。

translations.literal: If one hears them out, accusation and expose never end; if one forbids utterly, encroachment and wrong know no limit—compared with the trouble of managing lawsuits, still better than the harm of encroachment and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Hear every appeal and informers never rest; ban complaints and injustice runs wild—better the fuss of courts than unchecked wrong.

sentences.zh: 今禁訟訴，則杜一國之口，培一人之勢，使得縱橫，無所顧憚。

translations.literal: Now banning lawsuits and appeals then stops the mouths of a whole state, heaps up one man's power, lets him range unchecked with nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Banning appeals gags a province and swells one man's power until he acts without scruple.

sentences.zh: 諸受枉者抱怨積直，獨不蒙天地無私之德，而長壅蔽於邪人之銓。

translations.literal: All who suffer wrong harbor resentment and pile up grievance; alone they do not receive the virtue of Heaven and Earth's selflessness, but long are blocked and screened by the wicked man's evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: The wronged nurse rage yet never see impartial Heaven—they stay trapped beneath crooked graders.

sentences.zh: 使上明不下照，下情不上聞。

translations.literal: This causes enlightened clarity above not to shine below; feelings below not to be heard above.
translations.idiomatic: So clarity never reaches below and truth never rises above.

sentences.zh: 損政之道四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth way it harms governance.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fourth wound to good rule.

sentences.zh: 昔在前聖之世，欲敦風俗，鎮靜百姓，隆鄉黨之義，崇六親之行，禮教庠序以相率，賢不肖於是見矣。

translations.literal: In former ages of prior sages, desiring to enrich custom and calm the hundred surnames, they raised village fellowship and honored six-kins conduct; ritual teaching and schools led one another—worthy and unworthy thereby appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sages steadied custom by exalting village ties and kinship ritual—schools spread pattern, and talent showed plain.

sentences.zh: 然鄉老書其善以獻天子，司馬論其能以官於職，有司考績以明黜陟。

translations.literal: Then village elders wrote their goodness and presented it to the Son of Heaven; the minister of war debated their ability and officered them to posts; responsible offices examined merit to clarify demotion and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Elders recorded virtue for the throne; the bureau matched skill to office; ministries audited performance for promotions.

sentences.zh: 故天下之人退而修本，州黨有德義，朝廷有公正，浮華邪佞無所容厝。

translations.literal: Therefore men of all under Heaven withdrew and cultivated root; in district and village were virtue and right; at court was fairness and justice—florid display and wicked flattery had nowhere to lodge.
translations.idiomatic: So men cultivated themselves at home, villages kept moral debt straight, court judgments stayed fair, and poseurs found no foothold.

sentences.zh: 今一國之士多者千數，或流徙異邦，或取給殊方，面猶不識，況盡其才力！

translations.literal: Now the gentlemen of one state number at most in thousands—some drift and migrate to foreign lands, some draw supplies from distant regions; faces they still do not recognize—how much less exhaust their talents and strength!
translations.idiomatic: Today a circuit may hold a thousand candidates—some wander abroad, some serve far away—clerks cannot know their faces, let alone their gifts.

sentences.zh: 而中正知與不知，其當品狀，采譽於台府，納毀於流言。

translations.literal: Yet the impartial judge knows or does not know; when fixing rank and description, he gathers praise from the terrace offices, admits slander from floating rumor.
translations.idiomatic: Graders know some men and miss others; profiles crib palace gossip and street slander.

sentences.zh: 任己則有不識之蔽，聽受則有彼此之偏。

translations.literal: Trusting himself then there is the screening of not knowing; listening and accepting then there is partiality of each side.
translations.idiomatic: Trust himself and he blinds himself; trust rumor and faction pulls him.

sentences.zh: 所知者以愛憎奪其平，所不知者以人事亂其度；

translations.literal: Those he knows—love and hate steal their fairness; those he does not know—human maneuvering disorders his measure;
translations.idiomatic: Men he favors bend his scales; strangers fall prey to backstage deals;

sentences.zh: 既無鄉老紀行之譽，又非朝廷考績之課；

translations.literal: Since there is neither village elders' praise recording conduct nor court examination of merit;
translations.idiomatic: They lack elder appraisals and palace merit audits;

sentences.zh: 遂使進宮之人，棄近求遠，背本逐末。

translations.literal: thereby they cause men advancing into court to abandon the near and seek the far, turn back from root and chase the tip.
translations.idiomatic: so candidates forsake home ties for distant patrons and chase reputation over substance.

sentences.zh: 位以求成，不由行立，品不校功，黨譽虛妄。

translations.literal: Rank through seeking success—not through conduct established; grades do not verify merit—faction praise is empty and false.
translations.idiomatic: Office follows lobbying, not behavior; ranks ignore results; clique praise lies hollow.

sentences.zh: 損政五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth harm to governance.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fifth scourge on government.

sentences.zh: 凡所以立品設狀者，求人才以理物也，非虛飾名譽，相為好醜。

translations.literal: In general the purpose of establishing grades and setting descriptions is to seek talented men to order things—not vainly to adorn reputation and mutually play at liking or disliking.
translations.idiomatic: Profiles exist to place talent for governing things—not to varnish reputations or swap favors.

sentences.zh: 雖孝悌之行，不施朝廷，故門外之事，以義斷恩。

translations.literal: Though conduct of filial piety and fraternal duty is not displayed at court, therefore matters outside the gate—by rightness sever favor.
translations.idiomatic: Filial duty belongs at home; outside the gate right overrides kinship.

sentences.zh: 既以在官，職有大小，事有劇易，各有功報，此人才之實效，功分之所得也。

translations.literal: Once in office, posts have large and small; affairs have arduous and easy—each has merit returned—this is the real effect of talent, what merit allotment obtains.
translations.idiomatic: In office, duties differ in weight and strain—each post earns its outcome; that is measurable merit.

sentences.zh: 今則反之，於限當報，雖職之高，還附卑品，無績於官，而獲高敘，是為抑功實而隆虛名也。

translations.literal: Now it is reversed: within the limit one ought to report—even though the post is high, still attach to low grade; without merit in office yet obtaining high rank—this is suppressing meritorious reality and elevating empty name.
translations.idiomatic: Today it runs backward: merit goes unrewarded—high office sinks low on the rolls while drones gain top ranks—real service starves while hollow fame thrives.

sentences.zh: 上奪天朝考績之分，下長浮華朋黨之士。

translations.literal: Above it steals the allotment of court merit examination; below it lengthens florid faction gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Above it steals the court's power to judge merit; below it breeds flashy coteries.

sentences.zh: 損政六也。

translations.literal: This is the sixth harm to governance.
translations.idiomatic: That is the sixth injury to the state.

sentences.zh: 凡官不同事，人不同能，得其能則成，失其能則敗。

translations.literal: In general offices differ in affairs; men differ in ability—obtain the matching ability then success; lose the matching ability then failure.
translations.idiomatic: Posts demand different skills; match skill to seat and rule thrives—mismatch and it fails.

sentences.zh: 今品不狀才能之所宜，而以九等為例。

translations.literal: Now grades do not describe what abilities suit them, yet take the nine ranks as pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Profiles no longer map talent to tasks—they ape nine pigeonholes.

sentences.zh: 以品取人，或非才能之所長；

translations.literal: Taking men by grade—perhaps it is not what their ability excels at;
translations.idiomatic: Grade-driven picks may miss a man's true strength;

sentences.zh: 以狀取人，則為本品之所限。

translations.literal: taking men by description—then one is limited by this grade itself.
translations.idiomatic: profile-driven picks stay chained to the original rank.

sentences.zh: 若狀得其實，猶品狀相妨，系縶選舉，使不得精於才宜。

translations.literal: If the description obtains the truth, still grade and description obstruct each other, tie and bind selection and recommendation, making one unable to refine to suitability of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Even accurate profiles clash with grades and throttle appointments until fit is guesswork.

sentences.zh: 況今九品，所疏則削其長，所親則飾其短。

translations.literal: How much more now the nine ranks—those neglected then trim their strengths; those favored then adorn their shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: Worse still, graders slash rivals' gifts and varnish allies' flaws.

sentences.zh: 徒結白論，以為虛譽，則品不料能，百揆何以得理，萬機何以得修？

translations.literal: Merely knot empty discourse, taking it as hollow praise—then grades do not gauge ability—how can the hundred directors attain order, how can the myriad threads attain repair?
translations.idiomatic: Empty forms stack up as fame—grades blind to capacity—how may the ministries stay ordered or business stay sound?

sentences.zh: 損政七也。

translations.literal: This is the seventh harm to governance.
translations.idiomatic: That is the seventh ruin for rule.

sentences.zh: 前九品詔書，善惡必書，以為褒貶，當時天下，少有所忌。

translations.literal: The former nine-ranks edict—good and evil must be written, taken as praise and blame—at that time under Heaven few had things they feared.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier edicts logged good and evil for praise or blame—few under Heaven dared abuse the power.

sentences.zh: 今之九品，所下不彰其罪，所上不列其善，廢褒貶之義，任愛憎之斷，清濁同流，以植其私。

translations.literal: Now in the nine ranks, what is demoted does not display their crimes; what is promoted does not list their goodness—abolishing the meaning of praise and blame, trusting judgment of love and hate—clear and muddy flow together to plant private ends.
translations.idiomatic: Today's ranks hide faults below and virtues above—no praise or blame—judgment tracks spite until pure and foul merge for private gain.

sentences.zh: 故反違前品，大其形勢，以驅動眾人，使必歸己。

translations.literal: Therefore they overturn and violate prior grades, enlarge their posture of power, thereby to drive and move the multitude, making them surely submit to oneself.
translations.idiomatic: So they flout prior verdicts, swell their clout, herd everyone, and force clients into line.

sentences.zh: 進者無功以表勸，退者無惡以成懲。

translations.literal: Those promoted have no merit whereby to display encouragement; those demoted have no evil whereby to complete punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Promotions reward no virtue; demotions punish no vice.

sentences.zh: 懲勸不明，則風俗污濁，天下人焉得不解德行而銳人事？

translations.literal: When punishment and encouragement are unclear, then custom is filthy and turbid—how can men of all under Heaven not loosen virtue and sharpen human maneuvering?
translations.idiomatic: Unclear carrots and sticks foul custom—how will anyone prize character over lobbying?

sentences.zh: 損政八也。

translations.literal: This is the eighth harm to governance.
translations.idiomatic: That is the eighth calamity for government.

sentences.zh: 由此論之，選中正而非其人，授權勢而無嘗罰，或缺中正而無禁檢，故邪黨得肆，枉濫縱橫。

translations.literal: Judging by this discussion—selecting an impartial judge who is not the right man; granting power and momentum without rewards and punishments; or lacking an impartial judge without prohibition and inspection—therefore wicked factions get free rein; twisting and overflow range unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: Thus wrong men hold the rectifier's seat, power rides without accountability, or monitors vanish—factions run wild and injustice spreads.

sentences.zh: 雖職名中正，實為奸府；

translations.literal: Though the duty is named 'impartial judge,' in reality it is a bureau of wickedness;
translations.idiomatic: The title says impartial judge; the truth is a nest of intrigue;

sentences.zh: 事名九品，而有八損。

translations.literal: the affair is named nine ranks, yet has eight harms.
translations.idiomatic: the system boasts nine grades yet delivers eight wounds.

sentences.zh: 或恨結於親親，猜生於骨肉，當身困於敵讎，子孫離其殃咎。

translations.literal: Some hate knots among closest kin; suspicion arises between bone and flesh; their persons are trapped among foes and enemies; sons and grandsons suffer their calamities and blame.
translations.idiomatic: Kin turn to enemies, bones rankle against flesh, men rot amid vendettas, and posterity pays the price.

sentences.zh: 斯乃歷世之患，非徒當今之害也。

translations.literal: This is the affliction of successive ages—not merely the harm of the present.
translations.idiomatic: This curse spans dynasties—not a flaw of our moment alone.

sentences.zh: 是以時主觀時立法，防奸消亂，靡有常制，故周因于殷，有所損益。

translations.literal: Therefore timely lords observe the times and establish law, guard against wickedness and dissolve disorder—there is no constant system—therefore Zhou inherited from Yin with some reduction and increase.
translations.idiomatic: Wise rulers rewrite law for their hour to curb plotters—no code lasts forever—Zhou borrowed from Yin yet revised it.

sentences.zh: 至於中正九品，上聖古賢皆所不為，豈蔽於此事而有不周哉，將以政化之宜無取於此也。

translations.literal: As for impartial judges and nine ranks—supreme sages and ancient worthies all did not practice them—was it that they were screened on this matter and had incompleteness? It is that for the fitness of governing transformation there is nothing to take from this.
translations.idiomatic: Highest sages never used nine-grade rectifiers—not because they overlooked it but because sound rule needs nothing from it.

sentences.zh: 自魏立以來，未見其得人之功，而生讎薄之累。

translations.literal: From Wei's establishment onward, one has not seen its merit in gaining men, yet life-long hatred and meanness accumulate.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei invented it, talent gains are invisible while spite piles high.

sentences.zh: 毀風敗俗，無益於化，古今之失，莫大於此。

translations.literal: Ruining custom and defeating popular practice—it benefits transformation nothing—of ancient and modern failures none is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: It poisons morals and aids culture not at all—no policy ever failed worse.

sentences.zh: 愚臣以為宜罷中正，除九品，棄魏氏之弊法，立一代之美制。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant holds that one ought to abolish impartial judges, remove the nine ranks, cast aside Wei's flawed law, and establish a fine system for this generation.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant urges abolishing regional graders and nine ranks—discard Wei's broken statute and craft institutions worthy of this age.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，優詔答之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, a gracious edict replied.
translations.idiomatic: The throne answered with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 後司空衛瓘等亦共表宜省九品，復古鄉議里選。

translations.literal: Later Minister of Works Wei Guan and others jointly memorialized that one ought to reduce the nine ranks and restore ancient village deliberation and hamlet selection.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei Guan and others jointly urged cutting nine ranks and reviving village recommendation.

sentences.zh: 帝竟不施行。

translations.literal: The Emperor in the end did not implement it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor never acted on it.

sentences.zh: 毅夙夜在公，坐而待旦，言議切直，無所曲撓，為朝野之所式瞻。

translations.literal: Yi morning and night was at public duty, sitting while waiting for dawn; his speech and debate were keen and straight; nothing bent or twisted him—he was what court and wild modeled and gazed upon.
translations.idiomatic: Yi rose before dawn for office, spoke bluntly, bowed to no pressure, and became the standard court and countryside admired.

sentences.zh: 嘗散齋而疾，其妻省之，毅便奏加妻罪而請解齋。

translations.literal: Once during purification fast he fell ill; his wife visited him; Yi then memorialized to add his wife's offense and requested dissolution of the fast.
translations.idiomatic: During a purification fast he fell ill; when his wife visited he memorialized her trespass and asked to break the fast.

sentences.zh: 妻子有過，立加杖捶，其公正如此。

translations.literal: If wife or children had fault, immediately he applied beating with stick—his fairness was thus.
translations.idiomatic: He beat wife or children on the spot for fault—such was his severity.

sentences.zh: 然以峭直，故不至公輔。

translations.literal: Yet because he was steep and straight, therefore he did not reach minister and aide.
translations.idiomatic: His abrupt honesty barred him from chief counselor posts.

sentences.zh: 帝以毅清貧，賜錢三十萬，日給米肉。

translations.literal: The Emperor because Yi was pure and poor granted cash three hundred thousand, daily supplying grain and meat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, pitying his austerity, granted three hundred thousand cash plus daily rice and meat.

sentences.zh: 年七十，告老。

translations.literal: At age seventy he announced old age.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 久之，見許，以光祿大夫歸第，門施行馬，復賜錢百萬。

translations.literal: After long time permission was seen; as grand messenger at court he returned to his mansion; racing-chariot barriers were set at his gate; again cash a million was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually permitted, he retired as supernumerary minister with carriage rails before his gate and another million in silver.

sentences.zh: 後司徒舉毅為青州大中正，尚書以毅懸車致仕，不宜勞以碎務。

translations.literal: Later the Minister of Education nominated Yi as grand rectifier for Qingzhou; the Ministry of State Affairs held that Yi had hung up his carriage and retired from office—one ought not to weary him with petty affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The steward later nominated Yi as Qingzhou's chief rectifier; the ministry argued his carriage hung idle in retirement—petty chores ill suited him.

sentences.zh: 陳留相樂安孫尹表曰：「禮，凡卑者執勞，尊得居逸，是順敘之宜也。

translations.literal: Sun Yin of Le'an, Chancellor of Chenliu, memorialized: "By ritual, generally inferiors perform labor; superiors obtain ease—this is the fitness of obedient order."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yin of Chenliu wrote: "Rite bids inferiors bear toil and superiors enjoy ease—that is proper order."

sentences.zh: 司徒魏舒、司隸校尉嚴詢與毅年齒相近，往者同為散騎常侍，後分授外內之職，資途所經，出處一致。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Wei Shu, Metropolitan Governor Yan Xun, and Yi were near in age and teeth; formerly together they were regular attendants at casual riding; later they separately received outer and inner duties—what their qualifications and paths passed through, exit and entry were one pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu, Yan Xun, and Yi are peers—once fellow attendants, later split between inner and outer posts along parallel careers.

sentences.zh: 今詢管四十萬戶州，兼董司百僚，總攝機要，舒所統殷廣，兼執九品，銓十六州論議，主者不以為劇。

translations.literal: Now Xun governs a province of four hundred thousand households, concurrently supervises and directs the hundred officials, gathers and holds the pivot points; what Shu commands is vast and wide, concurrently holding the nine ranks, evaluating sixteen provinces' discussions—the chief does not deem this arduous.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xun runs a four-hundred-thousand-household circuit, audits the bureaucracy, and guards secrets; Wei Shu commands wider territory, grades nine ranks across sixteen provinces—nobody calls their burden light.

sentences.zh: 毅但以知一州，便謂不宜累以碎事，於毅太優，詢、舒太劣。

translations.literal: Yet because Yi only knows one province, then one says he ought not be burdened with petty matters—toward Yi this is too generous, toward Xun and Shu too harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yi may rate one province and you call that too tedious—sparing him insults Yan and Wei.

sentences.zh: 若以前聽致仕，不宜復與遷授位者，故光祿大夫鄭袤為司空是也。

translations.literal: If because formerly hearing retirement from office, one ought not again participate in promotion and conferral of rank—therefore Grand Messenger at Court Zheng Mao became Minister of Works—this is the case.
translations.idiomatic: If retirees must never take new posts, why did Zheng Mao rise to minister of works?

sentences.zh: 夫知人則哲，惟帝難之。

translations.literal: Now knowing men is wise—only the lord finds it hard.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing men is wisdom itself—even emperors stumble over it.

sentences.zh: 尚可復委以宰輔之任，不可諮以人倫之論，臣竊所未安。

translations.literal: Still one may again entrust him with minister and aide duties—one cannot consult him on judgments of human relations—your servant secretly finds this not settled.
translations.idiomatic: You would trust him with chief ministership yet deny him voice on human rankings—your servant finds that unsettling.

sentences.zh: 昔鄭武公年過八十，入為周司徒，雖過懸車之年，必有可用。

translations.literal: Of old Duke Wu of Zheng passed eighty years and entered as minister of education for Zhou—though past the age of hung carriage, surely there was usability.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wu of Zheng became Zhou's steward past eighty—beyond retiring age yet indispensable.

sentences.zh: 毅前為司隸，直法不撓，當朝之臣，多所按劾。

translations.literal: Yi formerly was metropolitan governor—straight in law, unbending—many at court he impeached and examined.
translations.idiomatic: Yi headed the metropolitan office—inflexible in law—and impeached hosts of sitting ministers.

sentences.zh: 諺曰：'受堯之誅，不能稱堯。

translations.literal: A proverb says: 'Those who suffer Yao's punishment cannot praise Yao.'
translations.idiomatic: The proverb runs: "Men you punish will not sing your praises like Yao."

sentences.zh: '直臣無黨，古今所悉。

translations.literal: ' Straight ministers have no faction—ancient and modern know this fully.
translations.idiomatic: Straight ministers keep no clique—always thus."

sentences.zh: 是以汲黯死于淮陽，董仲舒裁為諸侯之相。

translations.literal: Therefore Ji An died in Huaiyang; Dong Zhongshu was reduced to be chancellor of a feudal lord.
translations.idiomatic: So Ji An died in provincial exile and Dong Zhongshu sank to tutoring a prince.

sentences.zh: 而毅獨遭聖明，不離輦轂，當世之士咸以為榮。

translations.literal: Yet Yi alone encountered sagely clarity, not leaving the imperial carriage hub—men of the age all took this as glory.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yi alone stayed beside the capital carriages under an enlightened throne—the age counted him blessed.

sentences.zh: 毅雖身偏有風疾，而志氣聰明，一州品第，不足勞其思慮。

translations.literal: Although Yi's body partly has wind illness, his aspiration and breath are bright and wise—one province's grades and ranks do not suffice to weary his deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Though palsy wracks his frame, his mind stays lucid—grading one circuit hardly strains him.

sentences.zh: 毅疾惡之心小過，主者必疑其論議傷物，故高其優禮，令去事實，此為機閣毅，使絕人倫之路也。

translations.literal: Yi's heart of hating evil has slight excess; the chief surely suspects his discussions harm things—therefore they heighten his courteous treatment, making him depart from real affairs—this is to scheme and fence Yi in, making him cut off the road of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's zeal against vice border sharp; officials fear his verdicts wound men—so they heap empty honors to strip him of real duty, a bureaucratic snare that bars him from judging character.

sentences.zh: 臣州茂德惟毅，越毅不用，則清談倒錯矣。」

translations.literal: In our province the flourishing virtue is none but Yi—if Yi is passed over and not employed, then pure discussion will be overturned."
translations.idiomatic: Our circuit's finest talent is Yi alone—skip him and every honest verdict collapses."

sentences.zh: 於是青州自二品已上憑毅取正。

translations.literal: Thereupon in Qingzhou from second rank upward they relied on Yi for rectification.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter everyone from second rank up in Qingzhou accepted Yi as final arbiter.

sentences.zh: 光祿勳石鑒等共奏曰：「謹按陳留相孫尹表及與臣等書如左。

translations.literal: Superintendent of the Household Shi Jian and others jointly memorialized: "We respectfully attach Chancellor Sun Yin's memorial of Chenliu and his letters to us as follows.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Shi Jian and colleagues memorialized: "We append Prefect Sun Yin's papers herewith.

sentences.zh: 臣州履境海岱，而參風齊、魯，故人俗務本，而世敦德讓，今雖不充於舊，而遺訓猶存，是以人倫歸行，士識所守也。

translations.literal: Our province treads the coast of sea and Mount Dai and shares the manners of Qi and Lu—therefore custom attends to root while generations honor yielding virtue; though today it does not fill the old measure, surviving instructions remain—therefore human relations return to conduct and gentlemen know what they guard.
translations.idiomatic: Our land skirts sea and Tai and breathes Qi-Lu culture—people cling to subsistence and ritual yielding; though faded, ancient lessons linger, so moral order holds and scholars keep their standards.

sentences.zh: 前被司徒符，當參舉州大中正。

translations.literal: Formerly we received the Minister of Education's tally—we ought jointly to nominate the grand rectifier for the province.
translations.idiomatic: The steward's warrant charged us to nominate the provincial chief rectifier.

sentences.zh: 僉以光祿大夫毅，純孝至素，著在鄉閭。

translations.literal: All agreed on Grand Messenger at Court Yi—pure filial piety utmost plainness—manifest in village lanes.
translations.idiomatic: All backed Yi—pure grief at home, famed through every lane.

sentences.zh: 忠允亮直，竭於事上，仕不為榮，惟期盡節。

translations.literal: Loyal, fair, bright, and straight—he exhausts himself serving superiors; office he does not treat as glory—only expects to fulfill integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He serves superiors to exhaustion without craving glory—only duty matters.

sentences.zh: 正身率道，崇公忘私，行高義明，出處同揆。

translations.literal: He rectifies himself and leads the Way, exalts public and forgets private—conduct high, righteousness bright—exit and entry share one measure.
translations.idiomatic: He sets the example, prefers public good over private gain, and walks what he preaches.

sentences.zh: 故能令義士宗其風景，州閭歸其清流。

translations.literal: Therefore he can make righteous gentlemen model themselves on his bearing; districts submit to his clear current.
translations.idiomatic: Men of principle imitate him; villages rally to his upright judgment.

sentences.zh: 雖年耆偏疾，而神明克壯，實臣州人士所思准系者矣。

translations.literal: Though aged and partly ill, yet spirit and insight overcome robust—truly he is whom our province's people take as their mooring.
translations.idiomatic: Old and partly sick, his mind stays fierce—the circuit stakes its standards on him.

sentences.zh: 誠以毅之明格，能不言而信，風之所動，清濁必偃，以稱一州咸同之望故也。

translations.literal: Truly because Yi's bright standard can command belief without words—wherever his wind moves, clear and muddy surely yield—it meets one province's unanimous hope.
translations.idiomatic: His moral clarity needs no speeches—where his breeze blows, foul and fair bend—and that suits every expectation in the province.

sentences.zh: 竊以為禮賢尚德，教之大典，王制奪與，動為開塞，而士之所歸，人倫為大。

translations.literal: Your servant privately thinks honoring worthies and esteeming virtue is the great canon of teaching; royal regulation grants and withholds—movement opens or blocks—but what gentlemen return to—human relations are greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring talent anchors education; royal decrees open or close careers—yet nothing outweighs ordering society.

sentences.zh: 臣等虛劣，雖言廢於前，今承尹書，敢不列啟。

translations.literal: We ministers are empty and weak—though our words were set aside before—now receiving Yin's letter—how dare we not report.
translations.idiomatic: We are mean advisors whose plea failed once—Yin's letter leaves us no choice but to memorialize again.

sentences.zh: 按尹所執，非惟惜名議於毅之身，亦通陳朝宜奪與大准。

translations.literal: Examining what Yin upholds—not only does he cherish reputation for Yi's person—he also broadly states what court ought grant and withhold as great norm.
translations.idiomatic: Yin speaks not only for Yi's reputation—he lays out how the throne should grant or withhold rank in principle.

sentences.zh: 以為尹言當否，應蒙評議。」

translations.literal: We hold whether Yin's words are apt ought to receive deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: His Excellency's argument deserves full debate."

sentences.zh: 由是毅遂為州都，銓正人流，清濁區別，其所彈貶，自親貴者始。

translations.literal: By this Yi became provincial rectifier—evaluating and rectifying the human stream—clear and muddy distinguished—those he impeached and demoted began from kin and nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Yi took the provincial seat, sorted candidates, split worthy from worthless, and struck kin and grandees first.

sentences.zh: 太康六年卒，武帝撫幾驚曰：「失吾名臣，不得生作三公！

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taikang he died; Emperor Wu stroked the armrest and said startled: "We have lost Our famed minister—cannot have him live to serve among the Three Dukes!
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taikang 6; Emperor Wu smacked the rail: "We lost a pillar—he never lived to join the Three Dukes!

sentences.zh: 」即贈儀同三司，使者監護喪事。

translations.literal: " Immediately posthumously conferred parity with the Three Offices; envoys supervised the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: They granted him parity with the Three Offices with courtiers overseeing his obsequies.

sentences.zh: 羽林左監北海王宮上疏曰：「中詔以毅忠允匪躬，贈班台司，斯誠聖朝考績以毅著勳之美事也。

translations.literal: Colonel of the Feathered Forest left guard, Wang Gong of Beihai, submitted a memorial: "The inner edict because Yi was loyal and fair without sparing himself grants Three Offices rank—this is truly the sagely court examining merit for Yi's manifest achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel Wang Gong wrote: "The palace honors Yi's loyalty—posthumous Three Offices rank crowns real service.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按，諡者行之跡，而號者功之表。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully examines—posthumous title is the trace of conduct—while honorific title is the showing of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous names record conduct; noble titles record deeds.

sentences.zh: 今毅功德並立，而有號無諡，於義不體。

translations.literal: Now Yi's merit and virtue both stand—yet he has title without posthumous name—in righteousness not a proper body.
translations.idiomatic: Yi earned both virtue and achievement yet lacks a posthumous name—that breaks precedent.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以《春秋》之事求之，諡法主於行而不系爵。

translations.literal: Your servant privately seeks it in Spring and Autumn affairs—posthumous law masters conduct and does not tie to noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn ties posthumous names to deeds, not to pedigree.

sentences.zh: 然漢、魏相承，爵非列侯，則皆沒而高行，不加之諡，至使三事之賢臣，不如野戰之將。

translations.literal: Yet Han and Wei inherit—if rank is not ranked marquis then all die with high conduct—none adds posthumous title—until worthy ministers of the Three Departments prove less honored than wild campaign generals.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei withheld posthumous praise from anyone below full marquis—so loyal ministers ranked beneath battlefield brutes.

sentences.zh: 銘跡所殊，臣願聖世舉《春秋》之遠制，改列爵之舊限，使夫功行之實不相掩替，則莫不率賴。

translations.literal: What inscription traces distinguish—your servant wishes the sagely age would raise Spring and Autumn's distant system—alter the old limit of ranked nobility—so that merit and conduct's reality do not obscure each other—then none would fail to depend.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant asks this court to revive ancient naming rules so merit matches tribute—none would doubt Your fairness.

sentences.zh: 若以革舊毀制，非所倉卒，則毅之忠益，雖不攻城掠地，論德進爵，亦應在例。

translations.literal: If because altering old destroys regulation—not something for haste—then Yi's loyal benefit—even though not storming cities or plundering lands—debating virtue advancing rank—also ought to fall within precedent.
translations.idiomatic: If reform cannot come overnight, Yi's steadfast counsel—though no conqueror—still merits posthumous grace by precedent.

sentences.zh: 臣敢惟行甫請周之義，謹牒毅功行如石。

translations.literal: Your servant dares follow Xingfu's meaning in begging Zhou—respectfully presenting Yi's merit and conduct as stone.
translations.idiomatic: Following the precedent of humble memorials to Zhou, Your servant lists Yi's deeds below.

sentences.zh: 」帝出其表使八坐議之，多同宮議。

translations.literal: " The Emperor produced his memorial and had the Eight Seats debate—most agreed with Gong's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor circulated Wang Gong's text to the Eight Seats—most concurred.

sentences.zh: 奏寢不報。

translations.literal: Memorial submitted—slept—no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial vanished into silence—no answer came.

sentences.zh: 二子：暾、總。

translations.literal: Two sons: Tun and Zong.
translations.idiomatic: He left two sons: Liu Tun and Liu Zong.

translations.literal: Equals sign (scribal section marker in source).
translations.idiomatic: (Section marker.)

sentences.zh: 子暾

translations.literal: His son Tun
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Tun

sentences.zh: =暾字長升，正直有父風。

translations.literal: =Tun courtesy name Changsheng—upright with his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tun, styled Changsheng, was blunt like his father.

sentences.zh: 太康初為博士，會議齊王攸之國，加崇典禮，暾與諸博士坐議迕旨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taikang he became erudite; when they convened on Prince of Qi You's fief—raising ceremonial honors—Tun with the other erudites sat debating and offended the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taikang he served as erudite; debating Prince You's investiture he challenged imperial policy with his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 武帝大怒，收暾等付廷尉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was greatly angry—seized Tun and others and handed them to the commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu jailed Tun and the classicists in the ministry of justice.

sentences.zh: 會赦得出，免官。

translations.literal: When an amnesty occurred they obtained release—removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty freed him but stripped his post.

sentences.zh: 初，暾父毅疾馮紞奸佞，欲奏其罪，未果而卒。

translations.literal: Earlier Tun's father Yi despised Feng Dan's wicked flattery—wished to memorialize his crimes—did not succeed before dying.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi had meant to impeach Feng Dan but died first.

sentences.zh: 至是，紞位宦日隆，暾慨然曰：「使先人在，不令紞得無患。」

translations.literal: At this point Dan's position and favor grew daily—Tun sighed and said: "If my late father still lived he would not let Dan escape trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Now Feng Dan flourished; Tun muttered that his father would never have spared him.

sentences.zh: 後為酸棗令，轉侍御史。

translations.literal: Later he became magistrate of Suanzao—transferred to attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Suanzao, then joined the censorate.

sentences.zh: 會司徒王渾主簿劉輿獄辭連暾，將收付廷尉。

translations.literal: When Minister of Education Wang Hun's clerk Liu Yu's prison testimony linked Tun—they were about to seize him for the commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's confession tied Tun to Wang Hun's bureau scandal—arrest loomed.

sentences.zh: 渾不欲使府有過，欲距劾自舉之。

translations.literal: Hun did not wish his bureau to have fault—wished to refuse impeachment and recommend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun feared blame on his office and tried to preempt the charge himself.

sentences.zh: 與暾更相曲直，渾怒，便遜位還第。

translations.literal: He and Tun exchanged blame—Hun angry—then yielded his seat and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: They quarreled until Wang Hun quit his post in fury.

sentences.zh: 暾乃奏渾曰：「謹按司徒王渾，蒙國厚恩，備位鼎司，不能上佐天子，調和陰陽，下遂萬物之宜，使卿大夫各得其所。

translations.literal: Tun then memorialized Hun: "Your servant respectfully examines Minister of Education Wang Hun—receiving the state's deep grace—occupying the tripod ministers' place—unable above to aid the Son of Heaven and harmonize yin and yang—below to follow the myriad things' fitness—making ministers and grandees each obtain their station.
translations.idiomatic: Tun impeached Wang Hun for failing as steward—neither tuning cosmos nor sorting officers.

sentences.zh: 敢因劉輿拒扞詔使，私欲大府興長獄訟。

translations.literal: He dares rely on Liu Yu to resist imperial envoys—privately desires the great bureau to breed lengthy lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: He abused Liu Yu's case to stall envoys and breed lawsuits from his ministry.

sentences.zh: 昔陳平不答漢文之問，邴吉不問死人之變，誠得宰相之體也。

translations.literal: Of old Chen Ping did not answer Emperor Wen's question—Bing Ji did not ask about dead men's omens—truly grasping a chancellor's body.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ping kept silent before Emperor Wen; Bing Ji ignored roadside corpses—true chief ministers know their scope.

sentences.zh: 既興刑獄，怨懟而退，舉動輕速，無大臣之節，請免渾官。

translations.literal: Having stirred lawsuits—resentful withdrawal—movement light and swift—without great ministers' bearing—request removal of Hun's office.
translations.idiomatic: Having stirred courts then storming off—hardly ministerial conduct—strip Wang Hun's post.

sentences.zh: 右長史、楊丘亭侯劉肇，便辟善柔，苟于阿順，請大鴻臚削爵土。

translations.literal: Right chief clerk Marquis of Yangqiu Pavilion Liu Zhao—nimble obsequiousness and smooth softness—conniving at flattery—request the grand herald strip rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Liu Zhao—slick and servile—strip his title through the herald.

sentences.zh: 」諸聞暾此奏者，皆歎美之。

translations.literal: " All who heard Tun's memorial praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who read Tun's memorial applauded.

sentences.zh: 其後武庫火，尚書郭彰率百人自衛而不救火，暾正色詰之。

translations.literal: Later the armory burned—Minister Guo Zhang led a hundred men guarding himself but did not fight the fire—Tun sternly questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: When the arsenal caught fire Guo Zhang mustered guards for himself instead of buckets—Tun challenged him.

sentences.zh: 彰怒曰：「我能截君角也。

translations.literal: Zhang angrily said: "I can cut off your horn."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhang sneered that he could clip Tun's cap horn.

sentences.zh: 」暾勃然謂彰曰：「君何敢恃寵作威作福，天子法冠而欲截角乎！

translations.literal: " Tun bristling said to Zhang: "How dare you rely on favor to lord it—while wearing the Son of Heaven's legal cap you would cut the horn!
translations.idiomatic: Tun thundered back that favorites dare not mangle the imperial cap badge.

sentences.zh: 」求紙筆奏之，彰伏不敢言，眾人解釋，乃止。

translations.literal: " He sought paper and brush and memorialized—Zhang cowered speechless—the crowd mediated—then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted an impeachment on the spot—Guo Zhang shrank mute until peers smoothed things over.

sentences.zh: 彰久貴豪侈，每出輒眾百餘人。

translations.literal: Zhang long noble and extravagant—each outing always over a hundred followers.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhang traveled with a hundred retainers for show.

sentences.zh: 自此之後，務從簡素。

translations.literal: From this afterward he strove to follow simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: After Tun's rebuke he thinned his retinue.

sentences.zh: 暾遷太原內史，趙王倫篡位，假征虜將軍，不受，與三王共舉義。

translations.literal: Tun promoted to interior steward of Taiyuan—Prince Zhao Lun usurped—false general Who Subdues Caitiffs—he did not accept—joined the Three Princes in righteous rising.
translations.idiomatic: Made Taiyuan steward, he refused usurper Lun's general's baton and marched with the allied princes.

sentences.zh: 惠帝復阼，暾為左丞，正色立朝，三台清肅。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui restored the throne—Tun became left aide—stern dignity at court—the Three Terraces pure and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Under restored Emperor Hui he served as left aide—grim propriety quieted the three bureaus.

sentences.zh: 尋兼御史中丞，奏免尚書僕射、東安公繇及王粹、董艾等十餘人。

translations.literal: Soon concurrently palace secretary—memorialized removal of vice director of the right Prince of Dong'an You—Wang Cui—Dong Ai and over ten others.
translations.idiomatic: He soon impeached Wang Yun—Wang Cui—Dong Ai and a dozen more.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，遂即真。

translations.literal: Court praised him—then confirmed full tenure.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved and confirmed his posts.

sentences.zh: 遷中庶子、左衛將軍、司隸校尉，奏免武陵王澹及何綏、劉坦、溫畿、李晅等。

translations.literal: Promoted heir-adjunct—colonel of the left guard—metropolitan governor—memorialized removal of Prince of Wuling Dan—He Sui—Liu Tan—Wen Ji—Li Xuan and others.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to heir adviser—left guard colonel—metropolitan governor—and cashiered Prince Dan and several ministers.

sentences.zh: 長沙王乂討齊王冏，暾豫謀，封朱虛縣公，千八百戶。

translations.literal: Prince of Changsha Yi attacked Prince of Qi Jiong—Tun planned beforehand—ennobled duke of Zhuxu—one thousand eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He helped Prince Yi against Prince Jiong and earned a Zhuxu dukedom with eighteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 乂死，坐免。

translations.literal: Yi died—by association dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi fell Tun lost office too.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復為司隸。

translations.literal: Shortly—again metropolitan governor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned as metropolitan governor.

sentences.zh: 及惠帝之幸長安也，留暾守洛陽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui went to Chang'an—left Tun to guard Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui fled west—Tun stayed to hold Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒遣使鴆羊皇后，暾乃與留台僕射荀藩、河南尹周馥等上表，理后無罪。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Yong sent agents to poison Empress Yang—Tun with caretaker minister Xun Fan—Henan governor Zhou Fu memorialized her innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong tried to poison Empress Yang—Tun joined Xun Fan and Zhou Fu to plead her cause.

sentences.zh: 語在《后傳》。

translations.literal: Language is in Empress's biography.
translations.idiomatic: (See the "Biography of Empress Yang.")

sentences.zh: 顒見表，大怒，遣陳顏、呂朗率騎五千收暾，暾東奔高密王略。

translations.literal: Yong seeing the memorial raged—sent Chen Yan and Lu Lang with five thousand riders to seize Tun—Tun fled east to Prince of Gaomi Lue.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent riders to arrest Tun—who fled to Prince Lue.

sentences.zh: 會劉根作逆，略以暾為大都督，加鎮軍將軍討根。

translations.literal: When Liu Gen rebelled—Lue made Tun grand commander—added general Who Guards the Army to strike Gen.
translations.idiomatic: During Liu Gen's revolt Lue named Tun commander-in-chief to crush him.

sentences.zh: 暾戰失利，還洛。

translations.literal: Tun fought—lost—returned Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He lost and fell back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 至酸棗，值東海王越奉迎大駕。

translations.literal: Reaching Suanzao—met Prince of East Sea Yue welcoming the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: At Suanzao he met Prince Yue escorting the throne eastward.

sentences.zh: 及帝還洛，羊-{后}-反宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor returned Luoyang—Empress Yang returned palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor came home Empress Yang reentered the palace.

sentences.zh: -{后}-遣使謝暾曰：「賴劉司隸忠誠之志，得有今日。

translations.literal: Empress sent envoy thanking Tun: "We rely on Metropolitan Liu's loyal intent—we could reach today.
translations.idiomatic: The empress thanked Tun for loyalty that restored her.

sentences.zh: 」以舊勳復封爵，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: " By old merit again ennobled—added grand messenger at court.
translations.idiomatic: Her gratitude restored his fief and added a supernumerary minister title.

sentences.zh: 暾妻前卒，先陪陵葬。

translations.literal: Tun's wife died earlier—buried beside imperial tomb precinct.
translations.idiomatic: His wife predeceased him and lay in the tomb park.

sentences.zh: 子更生初婚，家法，婦當拜墓，攜賓客親屬數十乘，載酒食而行。

translations.literal: Son Gengsheng's first wedding—house rule—bride must bow at tomb—carrying guests and kin several tens of carriages—bearing wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: When son Gengsheng wed—custom demanded the bride bow at the tomb procession—dozens of carts with kin and wine.

sentences.zh: 先是，洛陽令王棱為越所信，而輕暾，暾每欲繩之，棱以為怨。

translations.literal: Earlier Luoyang magistrate Wang Ling trusted by Yue yet slighted Tun—Tun often wished to discipline him—Ling bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Wang Ling—Prince Yue's favorite—mocked Tun—who meant to impeach him—spawning spite.

sentences.zh: 時劉聰、王彌屯河北，京邑危懼。

translations.literal: At time Liu Cong and Wang Mi camped north of River—capital feared.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong and Wang Mi menaced the Yellow River—the capital panicked.

sentences.zh: 棱告越，雲暾與彌鄉親而欲投之。

translations.literal: Ling informed Yue—claiming Tun was Wang Mi's townsman and meant to defect.
