translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling told Yue that Tun—Wang Mi's fellow townsman—would desert.

sentences.zh: 越嚴騎將追暾，右長史傅宣明暾不然。

translations.literal: Yue ordered riders pursue Tun—right chief clerk Fu Xuan clarified Tun would not.
translations.idiomatic: Yue almost sent riders until Fu Xuan swore Tun innocent.

sentences.zh: 暾聞之，未至墓而反，以正義責越，越甚慚。

translations.literal: Tun hearing—before reaching tomb returned—with righteousness blamed Yue—Yue greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Tun turned back—rebuked Prince Yue—who flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 及劉曜寇京師，以暾為撫軍將軍、假節、都督城守諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Liu Yao raided capital—made Tun general Who Pacifies the Army—credential staff—supervisor of city defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao struck Luoyang Tun commanded defense as Pacifying Army general.

sentences.zh: 曜退，遷尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Yao withdrew—promoted vice director of the right.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao left Tun became vice director of the right.

sentences.zh: 越憚暾久居監司，又為眾情所歸，乃以為右光祿大夫，領太子少傅，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Yue feared Tun long holding inspector posts—also masses leaned on him—made him right grand messenger at court—concurrently junior tutor to heir—added regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue feared Tun's long tenure as censor—named him tutor and attendant to sideline real power.

sentences.zh: 外示崇進，實奪其權。

translations.literal: Outwardly showed honor advance—in reality seized his authority.
translations.idiomatic: The promotion looked grand—it stripped his authority.

sentences.zh: 懷帝又詔暾領衛尉，加特進。

translations.literal: Emperor Huai again ordered Tun oversee captain of the guards—added the Special Advancement dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai made him guard captain and conferred the Special Advancement title.

sentences.zh: 後復以暾為司隸，加侍中。

translations.literal: Later again made Tun metropolitan governor—added attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tun returned as metropolitan governor with palace attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 暾五為司隸，允協物情故也。

translations.literal: Tun five times metropolitan governor—because he matched popular sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: He served five tours as censor because the realm trusted him.

sentences.zh: 王彌入洛，百官殲焉。

translations.literal: Wang Mi entered Luoyang—hundred officials slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mi stormed Luoyang officials died wholesale.

sentences.zh: 彌以暾鄉里宿望，故免於難。

translations.literal: Mi because Tun hometown elder prestige—therefore spared disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi spared Tun out of hometown respect.

sentences.zh: 暾因說彌曰：「今英雄競起，九州幅裂，有不世之功者，宇內不容。

translations.literal: Tun therefore persuaded Mi: "Now heroes arise competing—nine provinces split apart—whoever lacks epochal merit finds no room within the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Tun urged Mi: "Warlords carve the realm—without supreme merit none survives.

sentences.zh: 將軍自興兵已來，何攻不克，何戰不勝，而復與劉曜不協，宜思文種之禍，以范蠡為師。

translations.literal: General since raising troops—which siege fails—which battle loses—yet again out of tune with Liu Yao—ought ponder Wen Zhong's fate—take Fan Li as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: You win every fight yet feud with Liu Yao—remember Wen Zhong's doom—study Fan Li's exit.

sentences.zh: 且將軍可無帝王之意，東王本州，以觀時勢，上可以混一天下，下可以成鼎峙之事，豈失孫、劉乎！

translations.literal: Moreover general may lack imperial ambition—eastward king your home province—watching the moment—above can unify below can forge tripod enterprise—would you lose Sun Quan and Liu Bei!
translations.idiomatic: Rule your native east—watch trends—unify or divide like Sun and Liu.

sentences.zh: 蒯通有言，將軍宜圖之。

translations.literal: Kuai Tong had words—general ought plan it.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai Tong said as much—consider it.

sentences.zh: 」彌以為然，使暾於青州，與曹嶷謀，且徵之。

translations.literal: " Mi agreed—sent Tun to Qingzhou—to scheme with Cao Yi—and summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi agreed—sent Tun east to bargain with Cao Yi.

sentences.zh: 暾至東阿，為石勒遊騎所獲，見彌與嶷書而大怒，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Tun reached Dong'e—captured by Shi Le's raiders—seeing Mi's letter to Yi—greatly angry—thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: At Dong'e Shi Le's scouts seized Tun—found Mi's letters—and executed him.

sentences.zh: 暾有二子：佑、白。

translations.literal: Tun had two sons: You and Bai.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors included sons Liu You and Liu Bai.

sentences.zh: 佑為太傅屬，白太子舍人。

translations.literal: You served Grand Tutor's staff—Bai heir-apparent attendant.
translations.idiomatic: You advised the grand tutor—Bai served the heir.

sentences.zh: 白果烈有才用，東海王越忌之，竊遣上軍何倫率百餘人入暾第，為劫取財物，殺白而去。

translations.literal: Bai forthright fierce talented—Prince of East Sea Yue envied him—secretly sent colonel He Lun with over a hundred men into Tun's mansion—pretending robbery taking goods—killed Bai and left.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue feared fiery Liu Bai—sent He Lun to loot Tun's house and murder Bai under cover of theft.

translations.literal: Equals sign (scribal section marker in source).
translations.idiomatic: (Section marker.)

sentences.zh: 子總

translations.literal: His son Zong
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Zong

sentences.zh: =總字弘紀，好學直亮，叔父彪，位至北軍中候。

translations.literal: =Zong courtesy name Hongji—loved learning straight bright—uncle Biao rose to colonel of northern army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zong styled Hongji—studious and blunt—his uncle Biao reached colonel of the northern armies.

sentences.zh: 程衛

translations.literal: Cheng Wei
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wei

sentences.zh: 程衛，字長玄，廣平曲周人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Wei, courtesy name Changxuan, was a native of Quzhou in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wei, styled Changxuan, came from Quzhou in Guangping.

sentences.zh: 少立操行，強正方嚴。

translations.literal: In youth he established conduct—forceful, upright, solemn.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was austere, blunt, and severe.

sentences.zh: 劉毅聞其名，辟為都官從事。

translations.literal: Liu Yi hearing his name summoned him as attendant clerk for capital crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi recruited him as clerk for metropolitan capital offenses.

sentences.zh: 毅奏中護軍羊琇犯憲應死。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized that Commander Who Guards the Army Yang Xiu violated statute—deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: Yi impeached Yang Xiu for breaking the law—a capital crime.

sentences.zh: 武帝與琇有舊，乃遣齊王攸喻毅，毅許之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu had old ties with Xiu—sent Prince of Qi You to persuade Yi—Yi assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, owing Yang Xiu a favor, had Prince You sway Yi—Yi relented.

sentences.zh: 衛正色以為不可，逕自馳車入護軍營，收琇屬吏，考問陰私，先奏琇所犯狼藉，然後言於毅。

translations.literal: Wei with stern color held it impossible—went straight driving carriage into the guards' camp—seized Xiu's subordinate clerks—examined hidden affairs—first memorialized Xiu's crimes in disorder—then reported to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wei refused, galloped into the guard camp, seized Yang Xiu’s staff, unearthed his secrets, and first reported the debacle to court—then told Yi.

sentences.zh: 由是名振遐邇，百官厲行。

translations.literal: Thereby his name shook far and near—the hundred officials sharpened conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His fame shook the realm—officials snapped to propriety.

sentences.zh: 遂辟公府掾，遷尚事郎、侍御史，在職皆以事幹顯。

translations.literal: Thereupon summoned as aide to the public bureau—promoted gentleman of the palace and attendant censor—in office always distinguished by handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the high bureau, rose through palace posts, and made his mark in every role.

sentences.zh: 補洛陽令，歷安定、頓丘太守，所蒞著績。

translations.literal: Supplemented as Luoyang magistrate—served as prefect of Anding and Dunqiu—wherever he arrived he showed merit.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Luoyang, Anding, and Dunqiu with a strong record.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: Died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in harness.

sentences.zh: 和嶠

translations.literal: He Jiao
translations.idiomatic: He Jiao

sentences.zh: 和嶠，字長輿，汝南西平人也。

translations.literal: He Jiao, courtesy name Changyu, was a native of Xiping in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He Jiao, styled Changyu, hailed from Xiping in Runan.

sentences.zh: 祖洽，魏尚書令。

translations.literal: Grandfather Qia—Wei minister of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather He Qia was Wei minister over the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 父逌，魏吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Father You—Wei minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His father He You held Wei’s ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 嶠少有風格，慕舅夏侯玄之為人，厚自崇重。

translations.literal: Jiao from youth had bearing—admired maternal uncle Xiahou Xuan’s person—greatly esteemed himself.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he carried himself like his uncle Xiahou Xuan—aloof and exacting.

sentences.zh: 有盛名于世，朝野許其能風俗，理人倫。

translations.literal: He had great fame in the world—court and wild approved his ability to move custom and order human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside praised him for shaping manners and moral order.

sentences.zh: 襲父爵上蔡伯，起家太子舍人。

translations.literal: Inherited father’s noble rank Baron of Shangcai—first office heir-apparent attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded the barony of Shangcai and entered service as heir‑apparent attendant.

sentences.zh: 累遷潁川太守，為政清簡，甚得百姓歡心。

translations.literal: Promoted repeatedly to prefect of Yingchuan—administration clear and simple—greatly won common people’s hearts.
translations.idiomatic: As Yingchuan prefect he ruled plainly and won the people.

sentences.zh: 太傅從事中郎庾敳見而歎曰：「嶠森森如千丈松，雖磥砢有節目，施之大廈，有棟樑之用。

translations.literal: Adjutant to the grand tutor Yu Ai saw him and sighed: "Jiao stands tall like a thousand-foot pine—though gnarled and knotty—applied to a great hall—has timber-and-beam use.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ai marveled: "He Jiao is a thousand‑foot pine—rough bark and all—yet palace timber.

sentences.zh: 」賈充亦重之，稱于武帝，入為給事黃門侍郎，遷中書令，帝深器遇之。

translations.literal: " Jia Chong also esteemed him—praised him to Emperor Wu—entered as gentleman attendant at the yellow gate—promoted director of the palace secretariat—Emperor deeply prized him.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong praised him to the throne; he entered the palace secretariat and became an imperial favorite.

sentences.zh: 舊監令共車入朝，時荀勖為監，嶠鄙勖為人，以意氣加之，每同乘，高抗專車而坐。

translations.literal: By old practice overseer and director shared carriage into court—at time Xun Xu was overseer—Jiao despised Xu’s person—applied spirit of pride—each time riding together—held head high and sat exclusive carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Overseer and director once rode together; Jiao scorned Xun Xu and insisted on a separate cart.

sentences.zh: 乃使監令異車，自嶠始也。

translations.literal: Thereupon made overseer and director different carriages—beginning with Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Separate carts for overseer and director began with He Jiao.

sentences.zh: 吳平，以參謀議功，賜弟郁爵汝南亭侯。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified—for planning merit—granted younger brother Yu noble rank Marquis of Runan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell he shared credit with his brother Yu, who gained a pavilion marquisate.

sentences.zh: 嶠轉侍中，愈被親禮，與任愷、張華相善。

translations.literal: Jiao transferred to palace attendant—more favored—in friendship with Ren Kai and Zhang Hua.
translations.idiomatic: As palace attendant he grew closer to the throne and befriended Ren Kai and Zhang Hua.

sentences.zh: 嶠見太子不令，因侍坐曰：「皇太子有淳古之風，而季世多偽，恐不了陛下家事。

translations.literal: Jiao seeing heir apparent was not sound—therefore sitting attendance said: "Crown prince has pure antique manner—but declining age abounds in sham—fears he cannot manage Your Majesty’s household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At leisure he warned that the crown prince seemed too rustic for a decadent age—unkind to the dynasty’s future.

sentences.zh: 」帝默然不答。

translations.literal: " Emperor silent—did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 後與荀顗、荀勖同侍，帝曰：「太子近入朝，差長進，卿可俱詣之，粗及世事。

translations.literal: Later together attending with Xun Yi and Xun Xu—Emperor said: "Heir apparent lately entered court—somewhat grown—you may all visit him—roughly touch on worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with the Xuns at his side, he told them to coach the heir on statecraft.

sentences.zh: 」即奉詔而還。

translations.literal: " Immediately obeyed edict and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 顗、勖並稱太子明識弘雅，誠如明詔。

translations.literal: Yi and Xu together praised heir apparent’s bright understanding—vast and refined—truly as enlightened edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yi and Xun Xu flattered the prince’s polish.

sentences.zh: 嶠曰：「聖質如初耳！

translations.literal: Jiao said: "Sagely substance like first!
translations.idiomatic: He Jiao said the heir had not improved a whit.

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅而起。

translations.literal: " Emperor displeased—rose.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rose in anger.

sentences.zh: 嶠退居，恆懷慨歎，知不見用，猶不能已。

translations.literal: Jiao withdrew—always harbored sighing regret—knew not employed—still could not stop.
translations.idiomatic: He brooded—knowing his counsel spurned yet unable to stay mute.

sentences.zh: 在御坐言及社稷，未嘗不以儲君為憂。

translations.literal: On imperial seat speaking of altars of soil and grain—never without taking heir as worry.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever talk touched the realm’s fate he fretted over the heir.

sentences.zh: 帝知其言忠，每不酬和。

translations.literal: Emperor knew his words loyal—each time did not respond in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew him faithful yet refused to engage.

sentences.zh: 後與嶠語，不及來事。

translations.literal: Later speaking with Jiao—did not reach future matters.
translations.idiomatic: Later audiences skirted the succession entirely.

sentences.zh: 或以告賈妃，妃銜之。

translations.literal: Someone informed Consort Jia—consort bore grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached Empress Jia—she nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 太康末，為尚書，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Late Taikang—became minister of state affairs—left office for mother’s mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taikang he headed the ministry until mourning his mother.

sentences.zh: 及惠帝即位，拜太子少傅，加散騎常侍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui mounted throne—appointed junior tutor to heir—added regular attendant at casual riding and grand messenger at court.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui he tutored the crown prince with added honorifics.

sentences.zh: 太子朝西宮，嶠從入。

translations.literal: Heir apparent attended western palace—Jiao followed within.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the heir to the western palace.

sentences.zh: 賈后使帝問嶠曰：「卿昔謂我不了家事，今日定云何？

translations.literal: Empress Jia had Emperor ask Jiao: "You once said I could not manage household affairs—today settled how?
translations.idiomatic: Through the emperor she taunted him about his old warning.

sentences.zh: 」嶠曰：「臣昔事先帝，曾有斯言。

translations.literal: " Jiao said: "Your servant formerly served late Emperor—once had this saying.
translations.idiomatic: He Jiao answered that he had warned Emperor Wu long ago.

sentences.zh: 言之不效，國之福也。

translations.literal: Words not fulfilled—state’s fortune.
translations.idiomatic: That it proved false was the realm’s luck.

sentences.zh: 臣敢逃其罪乎！

translations.literal: Your servant dare flee the blame!
translations.idiomatic: May he suffer if he shirked duty!

sentences.zh: 」卒，贈金紫光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，本位如前。

translations.literal: " At death posthumously gifted golden purple grand messenger—added gold seal purple ribbon—original rank as before.
translations.idiomatic: At death he received golden‑purple honors with seal and sash unchanged.

sentences.zh: 永平初，策諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Early Yongping—canon posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Early Yongping era he was canonized “Jian.”

sentences.zh: 嶠家產豐富，擬于王者，然性至吝，以是獲譏于世，杜預以為嶠有錢癖。

translations.literal: Jiao household property rich—rivaling kings—yet nature utmost stingy—thereby earned ridicule in the world—Du Yu thought Jiao had money mania.
translations.idiomatic: He rivaled princes in wealth yet was famously stingy—Du Yu called it coin‑counting mania.

sentences.zh: 以弟郁子濟嗣，位至中書郎。

translations.literal: Younger brother Yu’s son Ji succeeded—rank reached gentleman of the palace secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He adopted nephew Ji who rose to the secretariat.

translations.literal: Equals sign (scribal section marker in source).
translations.idiomatic: (Section break.)

sentences.zh: 弟郁

translations.literal: Younger brother Yu
translations.idiomatic: His brother He Yu

sentences.zh: =郁字仲輿，才望不及嶠，而以清幹稱，歷尚書左右僕射、中書令、尚書令。

translations.literal: =Yu courtesy name Zhongyu—talent and reputation did not match Jiao—but by clarity and efficiency praised—served vice director left and right of the ministry—director of palace secretariat—minister of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He Yu, styled Zhongyu, was leaner in fame than He Jiao but famed for efficiency—he rose to chief minister posts.

sentences.zh: 洛陽傾沒，奔于苟晞，疾卒。

translations.literal: Luoyang collapsed—fled to Gou Xi—died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell he fled to Gou Xi and died sick.

sentences.zh: 武陔

translations.literal: Wu Gai
translations.idiomatic: Wu Gai

sentences.zh: 武陔，字元夏，沛國竹邑人也。

translations.literal: Wu Gai, courtesy name Yuanxia, was a native of Zhuyi in Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Gai, styled Yuanxia, came from Zhuyi in Pei commandery.

sentences.zh: 父周，魏衛尉。

translations.literal: Father Zhou—Wei captain of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wu Zhou was Wei captain of the guards.

sentences.zh: 陔沈敏有器量，早獲時譽，與二弟韶叔夏、茂季夏並總角知名，雖諸父兄弟及鄉閭宿望，莫能覺其優劣。

translations.literal: Gai deep and keen with vessel capacity—early gained timely praise—with two younger brothers Shao Shuxia and Mao Jixia together known from hair-tied youth—though uncles, brothers, and village elders of long standing—none could perceive their better or worse.
translations.idiomatic: With brothers Shao and Mao he was celebrated since boyhood—even elders could not rank them.

sentences.zh: 同郡劉公榮有知人之鑒，常造周，周見其三子焉。

translations.literal: Same commandery Liu Gongrong had mirror for knowing men—often visited Zhou—Zhou showed him his three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gongrong of his county visited their father to judge the boys.

sentences.zh: 公榮曰：「皆國士也。

translations.literal: Gongrong said: "All are men of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Liu said all three were national talents.

sentences.zh: 元夏最優，有輔佐之才，陳力就列，可為亞公。

translations.literal: Yuanxia finest—has aide talent—deploying strength in rank—can be deputy to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxia topped them—ministerial timber next to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 叔夏、季夏不減常伯、納言也。」

translations.literal: Shuxia and Jixia not inferior to ordinary grandee or spokesman."
translations.idiomatic: The younger two matched senior ministers."

sentences.zh: 陔少好人倫，與潁川陳泰友善。

translations.literal: Gai from youth loved ordering human relations—with Yingchuan Chen Tai friendly.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Gai loved appraising talent and befriended Chen Tai.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝世，累遷下邳太守。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming of Wei’s age—promoted repeatedly to prefect of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei Mingdi he rose to Xiapi prefect.

sentences.zh: 景帝為大將軍，引為從事中郎，累遷司隸校尉，轉太僕卿。

translations.literal: Prince Jing as grand general—summoned as adjutant—promoted repeatedly metropolitan governor—transferred minister of the imperial stud.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing made him adjutant; he became metropolitan governor then minister of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 初封亭侯，五等建，改封薛縣侯。

translations.literal: First enfeoffed pavilion marquis—five ranks established—changed enfeoffment marquis of Xue county.
translations.idiomatic: First a pavilion lord, he became marquis of Xue under the new rank system.

sentences.zh: 文帝甚親重之，數與詮論時人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen deeply favored him—often debated men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen cherished him and debated character with him often.

sentences.zh: 嘗問陳泰孰若其父群，陔各稱其所長，以為群、泰略無優劣，帝然之。

translations.literal: Once asked Chen Tai compared to his father Qun—Gai praised each’s strengths—held Qun and Tai roughly without better or worse—Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: Asked to compare Chen Tai to Chen Qun, Wu Gai praised both equally—Wen agreed.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，拜尚書，掌吏部，遷左僕射、左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Taishi beginning—appointed minister of state affairs—presiding personnel—promoted vice director left—left grand messenger at court—opening office parity with Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Early Taishi he ran personnel, rose to vice director, grand messenger, and Three Offices parity.

sentences.zh: 陔以宿齒舊臣，名位隆重，自以無佐命之功，又在魏已為大臣，不得已而居位，深懷遜讓，終始全潔，當世以為美談。

translations.literal: Gai as elder veteran minister—name and position weighty—himself thinking no merit aiding founding—and already great minister in Wei—had no choice but occupy post—deeply harbored yielding humility—beginning to end whole pure—contemporaries took as fine tale.
translations.idiomatic: An elder statesman without founding laurels, he stayed humble in Wei-Jin transition—admired for unstained dignity.

sentences.zh: 卒於位，諡曰定。

translations.literal: Died in post—posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as “Ding.”

sentences.zh: 子輔嗣。

translations.literal: Son Fu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wu Fu inherited.

translations.literal: Equals sign (scribal section marker in source).
translations.idiomatic: (Section break.)

sentences.zh: 弟韶

translations.literal: Younger brother Shao
translations.idiomatic: His brother Wu Shao

sentences.zh: =韶歷吏部郎、太子右衛率、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: =Shao served minister of personnel gentleman—colonel right guard of heir—regular attendant at casual riding.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shao rose through personnel, heir guard colonel, and attendant posts.

translations.literal: Equals sign (scribal section marker in source).
translations.idiomatic: (Section break.)

sentences.zh: 弟茂

translations.literal: Younger brother Mao
translations.idiomatic: His brother Wu Mao

sentences.zh: =茂以德素稱，名亞於陔，為上洛太守、散騎常侍、侍中、尚書。

translations.literal: =Mao by plain virtue praised—name second to Gai—prefect of Shangluo—regular attendant at casual riding—attendant-in-ordinary—minister of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mao, famed for plain virtue just below Wu Gai, governed Shangluo and reached the ministries.

sentences.zh: 潁川荀愷年少於茂，即武帝姑子，自負貴戚，欲與茂交，距而不答，由是致怨。

translations.literal: Yingchuan Xun Kai younger than Mao—being Emperor Wu’s cousin by aunt—self-important as noble kin—wished befriend Mao—refused distance—thereby incurred resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The younger Xun Kai snubbed Wu Mao’s refusal of his patronizing friendship.

sentences.zh: 及楊駿誅，愷時為僕射，以茂駿之姨弟，陷為逆黨，遂見害。

translations.literal: When Yang Jun executed—Kai then vice director—because Mao Jun’s maternal nephew—trapped as rebel clique—thereupon harmed.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Jun fell, Xun Kai framed Wu Mao as Jun’s kin and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 茂清正方直，聞於朝野，一旦枉酷，天下傷焉。

translations.literal: Mao pure upright square straight—heard at court and wild—one morning twisted cruelty—world mourned.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mao’s wrongful death shocked the realm.

sentences.zh: 侍中傅祗上申明之，後追贈光祿勳。

translations.literal: Attendant Fu Zhi upward clarified—later posthumously gifted superintendent of the household.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi cleared his name and won posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 任愷

translations.literal: Ren Kai
translations.idiomatic: Ren Kai

sentences.zh: 任愷，字元褒，樂安博昌人也。

translations.literal: Ren Kai, courtesy name Yuanbao, was a native of Bochang in Le’an.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Kai, styled Yuanbao, came from Bochang in Le’an.

sentences.zh: 父昊，魏太常。

translations.literal: Father Hao—Wei minister of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ren Hao was Wei minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 愷少有識量，尚魏明帝女，累遷中書侍郎、員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Kai from youth had judgment and capacity—married Emperor Ming of Wei’s daughter—promoted repeatedly gentleman of the palace secretariat—supernumerary regular attendant at casual riding.
translations.idiomatic: He married a Wei princess and rose through secretariat and attendant posts.

sentences.zh: 晉國建，為侍中，封昌國縣侯。

translations.literal: When Jin state founded—palace attendant—enfeoffed marquis of Changguo county.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was founded he became palace attendant and marquis of Changguo.

sentences.zh: 愷有經國之幹，萬機大小多管綜之。

translations.literal: Kai had capacity for ordering the state—myriad threads small and large mostly managed comprehensively.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered statecraft large and small.

sentences.zh: 性忠正，以社稷為己任，帝器而昵之，政事多諮焉。

translations.literal: Nature loyal upright—took altars of soil and grain as self-task—Emperor prized and favored—state affairs mostly consulted.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal and blunt, he advised Emperor Wu on everything.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，鄭沖、王祥、何曾、荀顗、裴秀等各以老疾歸第。

translations.literal: Taishi beginning—Zheng Chong—Wang Xiang—He Zeng—Xun Yi—Pei Xiu each by old age illness returned mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Early Taishi the elder ministers retired ill.

sentences.zh: 帝優寵大臣，不欲勞以筋力，數遣愷諭旨于諸公，諮以當世大政，參議得失。

translations.literal: Emperor graciously favored great ministers—did not wish labor them with sinews—often sent Kai conveying intent to each lord—consulting on age’s great policies—debating gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: Wu sent Ren Kai to relay policy to the retired elders.

sentences.zh: 愷惡賈充之為人也，不欲令久執朝政，每裁抑焉。

translations.literal: Kai hated Jia Chong’s person—did not wish him long hold court governance—each time restrained.
translations.idiomatic: He worked to curb Jia Chong’s power.

sentences.zh: 充病之，不知所為。

translations.literal: Chong sick at heart—knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong despaired.

sentences.zh: 後承間言愷忠貞局正，宜在東宮，使護太子。

translations.literal: Later seizing interval spoke Kai loyal steadfast upright—ought be eastern palace—make protect heir.
translations.idiomatic: He urged posting Ren Kai to tutor the heir—ostensibly praise.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，以為太子少傅，而侍中如故，充計畫不行。

translations.literal: Emperor followed—thought junior tutor to heir—palace attendant as before—Chong’s plan did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Ren Kai heir tutor—blocking Jia’s scheme to exile rivals.

sentences.zh: 會秦、雍寇擾，天子以為憂。

translations.literal: When Qin and Yong raided and disturbed—Son of Heaven took as worry.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou and Yongzhou revolted—Wu fretted.

sentences.zh: 愷因曰：「秦、涼覆敗，關右騷動，此誠國家之所深慮。

translations.literal: Kai therefore said: "Qin and Liang overturned defeated—right of Pass disturbed—this truly state’s deep worry.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Kai called the northwest collapse dire.

sentences.zh: 宜速鎮撫，使人心有庇。

translations.literal: Ought quickly pacify soothe—make people’s hearts have shelter.
translations.idiomatic: It needed a credible marshal to reassure the west.

sentences.zh: 自非威望重臣有計略者，無以康西土也。

translations.literal: Unless prestige-weighted minister with stratagem—none can heal western lands.
translations.idiomatic: Only a heavyweight commander could calm it.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「誰可任者？

translations.literal: " Emperor said: "Who can be appointed?
translations.idiomatic: “Who fits?” asked the emperor.

sentences.zh: 」愷曰：「賈充其人也。

translations.literal: " Kai said: "Jia Chong is the man.
translations.idiomatic: “Jia Chong,” said Ren Kai—setting a trap.

sentences.zh: 」中書令庾純亦言之，於是詔充西鎮長安。

translations.literal: " Director of the palace secretariat Yu Chun also spoke—thereupon edict Chong west guard Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun echoed the call—so Jia Chong was ordered west.

sentences.zh: 充用荀勖計得留。

translations.literal: Chong using Xun Xu’s plan obtained stay.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong used Xun Xu’s ruse to remain at court.

sentences.zh: 充既為帝所遇，欲專名勢，而庾純、張華、溫顒、向秀、和嶠之徒皆與愷善，楊珧、王恂、華廙等充所親敬，於是朋黨紛然。

translations.literal: Chong having been favored by Emperor wished monopolize fame and power—while Yu Chun, Zhang Hua, Wen Yong, Xiang Xiu, He Jiao and their like all befriended Kai—Yang Yao, Wang Xun, Hua Yi and such Chong held dear—thereby faction cliques flared.
translations.idiomatic: Favored at court, Jia Chong craved control while Ren Kai moved with He Jiao and Zhang Hua—rival patrons split the faction map.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，召充、愷宴於式乾殿，而謂充等曰：「朝廷宜一，大臣當和。

translations.literal: Emperor knowing it—summoned Chong and Kai to feast at Shiqian Hall—and said to Chong and others: "Court ought be one—great ministers ought harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: Wu summoned both factions to Shiqian Hall and demanded unity.

sentences.zh: 」充、愷各拜謝而罷。

translations.literal: " Chong and Kai each bowed thanks and ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Both sides bowed off and left.

sentences.zh: 既而充、愷等以帝已知之而不責，結怨愈深，外相崇重，內甚不平。

translations.literal: Thereafter Chong, Kai and others because Emperor already knew yet did not blame—knot of hatred grew deeper—outwardly mutual esteem—innerly very unbalanced.
translations.idiomatic: Assured the throne would not punish them, Jia Chong and Ren Kai feigned respect while hating each other more.

sentences.zh: 或為充謀曰：「愷總門下樞要，得與上親接，宜啟令典選，便得漸疏，此一都令史事耳。

translations.literal: Someone for Chong schemed: "Kai governs privy-chamber pivot—gains close access to superiors—ought memorialize to make him superintend selection—then can gradually grow distant—this is one capital clerk’s affair.
translations.idiomatic: A counselor urged posting Ren Kai to personnel to edge him from the privy chamber.

sentences.zh: 且九流難精，間隙易乘。

translations.literal: Moreover nine currents hard to master—cracks easy to exploit.
translations.idiomatic: Nine grades invite slipups—easy targets for smears.

sentences.zh: 」充因稱愷才能，宜在官人之職。

translations.literal: " Chong therefore praised Kai’s talent—ought hold office of ordering men.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong praised Ren Kai’s fitness for personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝不之疑，謂充舉得其才。

translations.literal: Emperor did not suspect—said Chong’s recommendation obtained right talent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu trusted the nomination.

sentences.zh: 即日以愷為吏部尚書，加奉車都尉。

translations.literal: Same day appointed Kai minister of personnel—added commandant of palace carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Kai became minister of personnel with added military rank.

sentences.zh: 愷既在尚書，選舉公平，盡心所職，然侍覲轉希。

translations.literal: Kai already in ministry—selection fair—exhausted heart in duty—yet palace audiences grew rarer.
translations.idiomatic: He ran fair exams but rarely saw the emperor.

sentences.zh: 充與荀勖、馮紞承間浸潤，謂愷豪侈，用御食器。

translations.literal: Chong with Xun Xu, Feng Dan seizing intervals insinuated—claimed Kai extravagant—used imperial dining vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong, Xun Xu, and Feng Dan whispered that Ren Kai used imperial tableware.

sentences.zh: 充遣尚書右僕射、高陽王珪奏愷，遂免官。

translations.literal: Chong sent vice director of right Prince of Gaoyang Gui memorialize Kai—thereupon dismissed office.
translations.idiomatic: They had Prince Gui impeach him—Ren Kai lost his post.

sentences.zh: 有司收太官宰人檢核，是愷妻齊長公主得賜魏時御器也。

translations.literal: Responsible offices seized grand provisioner butchers and examined—it was Kai’s wife Princess Chang of Qi granted Wei-era imperial vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Investigators found only wedding gifts from Wei—Princess Chang’s old imperial vessels.

sentences.zh: 愷既免而譭謗益至，帝漸薄之。

translations.literal: Kai already dismissed yet slander increased—Emperor gradually slighted him.
translations.idiomatic: Vindicated yet still smeared, Ren Kai fell from favor.

sentences.zh: 然山濤明愷為人通敏有智局，舉為河南尹。

translations.literal: Yet Shan Tao clarified Kai’s person astute with wise capacity—recommended as governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao still named him Henan governor.

sentences.zh: 坐賊發不獲，又免官。

translations.literal: Sat because bandits rose—not captured—again dismissed office.
translations.idiomatic: He lost the post when bandits escaped capture.

sentences.zh: 復遷光祿勳。

translations.literal: Again promoted superintendent of the household.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as superintendent of the household.

sentences.zh: 愷素有識鑒，加以在公勤恪，甚得朝野稱譽。

translations.literal: Kai by nature had judgment—added to public diligence scrupulous—greatly won court and wild praise.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Kai’s discernment and diligence won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 而賈充朋黨又諷有司奏愷與立進令劉友交關。

translations.literal: Yet Jia Chong faction again hinted responsible offices memorialize Kai connected with Director of Stand-Fast Advance Liu You.
translations.idiomatic: Jia’s clique tied him to Prefect Liu You.

sentences.zh: 事下尚書，愷對不伏。

translations.literal: Matter sent to ministry—Kai replied not submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Kai pleaded innocent before the ministry.

sentences.zh: 尚書杜友、廷尉劉良並忠公士也，知愷為充所抑，欲申理之，故遲留而未斷，以是愷及友、良皆免官。

translations.literal: Minister Du You, commandant Liu Liang both loyal fair gentlemen—knew Kai suppressed by Chong—wished clarify—therefore delayed without deciding—thereby Kai and You and Liang all dismissed office.
translations.idiomatic: Du You and Liu Liang stalled to clear him—all three were cashiered.

sentences.zh: 愷既失職，乃縱酒耽樂，極滋味以自奉養。

translations.literal: Kai having lost office—thereupon indulged wine and pleasure—extreme flavors to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Out of office he drowned in wine and food.

sentences.zh: 初，何劭以公子奢侈，每食必盡四方珍饌，愷乃逾之，一食萬錢，猶云無可下箸處。

translations.literal: Earlier He Shao as noble son extravagant—each meal must exhaust four quarters’ rare delicacies—Kai then surpassed—one meal ten thousand cash—still said nowhere to place chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: He outspent He Shao’s legendary feasts—ten thousand cash per sitting yet claiming nothing worth eating.

sentences.zh: 愷時因朝請，帝或慰諭之，愷初無復言，惟泣而已。

translations.literal: Kai sometimes by court briefing—Emperor occasionally comforted instruct—Kai at first had no further words—only weeping.
translations.idiomatic: At audiences the emperor consoled him—Ren Kai could only weep.

sentences.zh: 後起為太僕，轉太常。

translations.literal: Later raised grand coachman—transferred minister of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as grand coachman then minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 初，魏舒雖歷位郡守，而未被任遇，愷為侍中，薦舒為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Earlier Wei Shu though repeatedly prefect—not yet met employment favor—Kai as palace attendant recommended Shu as regular attendant at casual riding.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Kai once lifted Wei Shu from obscurity to the attendant corps.

sentences.zh: 至是舒為右光祿、開府，領司徒，帝臨軒使愷拜授。

translations.literal: At this Shu was right grand messenger—opening office—heading minister of education—Emperor facing portico had Kai perform investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Now Wei Shu stood above him as minister—Emperor Wu made Ren Kai hand him the seal.

sentences.zh: 舒雖以弘量寬簡為稱，時以愷有佐世器局，而舒登三公，愷止守散卿，莫不為之憤歎也。

translations.literal: Shu though by vast capacity broad simplicity praised—men of time thought Kai had aid-the-age vessel—yet Shu ascended Three Dukes—Kai only guarded ordinary minister—none not for him indignant sigh.
translations.idiomatic: People resented that Shu surpassed the man who once sponsored him.

sentences.zh: 愷不得志，竟以憂卒，時年六十一，諡曰元，子罕嗣。

translations.literal: Kai unfulfilled in ambition—ended dying of grief—age sixty-one—posthumous title Yuan—son Han succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died heartsick at sixty-one—canonized Yuan—son Ren Han inherited.

translations.literal: Equals sign (scribal section marker in source).
translations.idiomatic: (Section break.)

sentences.zh: 子罕

translations.literal: Son Han
translations.idiomatic: His son Ren Han

sentences.zh: =罕字子倫，幼有門風，才望不及愷，以淑行致稱，為清平佳士。

translations.literal: =Han courtesy name Zilun—had family manner from youth—talent reputation did not reach Kai—by chaste conduct earned praise—was clear fair excellent gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Han, styled Zilun, lacked his father’s fame but won praise as a sober gentleman.

sentences.zh: 歷黃門侍郎、散騎常侍、兗州刺史、大鴻臚。

translations.literal: Served gentleman attendant at yellow gate—regular attendant at casual riding—inspector of Yanzhou—grand herald.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the palace to grand herald.

sentences.zh: 崔洪

translations.literal: Cui Hong
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong

sentences.zh: 崔洪，字良伯，博陵安平人也。

translations.literal: Cui Hong, courtesy name Liangbo, was native of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong, styled Liangbo, came from Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 高祖寔，著名漢代。

translations.literal: High ancestor Shi—famed in Han era.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestor Cui Shi was celebrated under the Han.

sentences.zh: 父贊，魏吏部尚書、左僕射，以雅量見稱。

translations.literal: Father Zan—Wei minister of personnel, vice director left—praised by spacious capacity.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cui Zan led Wei personnel and was famed for equanimity.

sentences.zh: 洪少以清厲顯名，骨鯁不同於物，人之有過，輒面折之，而退無後言。

translations.literal: Hong from youth by pure stern showed name—backbone straight different from things—when men had fault—then face rebuke—yet retiring no behind speech.
translations.idiomatic: He was blunt—scolding faults to one’s face yet silent behind backs.

sentences.zh: 武帝世，為御史治書。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu age—was editorial clerk for law.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu he served as legal editorial clerk.

sentences.zh: 時長樂馮恢父為弘農太守，愛少子淑，欲以爵傳之。

translations.literal: At time Changle Feng Hui’s father was prefect of Hongnong—loved youngest son Shu—wished transmit noble rank to him.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hui’s father planned to disinherit his heir for a younger son.

sentences.zh: 恢父終，服闋，乃還鄉里，結草為廬，陽喑不能言，淑得襲爵。

translations.literal: After father ended mourning—returned village—knotted grass into hut—feigned dumb unable speak—Shu obtained inherited noble.
translations.idiomatic: The heir feigned muteness in a grass hut so his brother stole the title.

sentences.zh: 恢始仕為博士祭酒，散騎常侍翟嬰薦恢高行邁俗，侔繼古烈。

translations.literal: Hui first took office as libationer of erudites—regular attendant Zhai Ying recommended Hui high conduct surpassing custom—match ancient stalwarts.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hui won praise as a rustic sage—Zhai Ying hailed him.

sentences.zh: 洪奏恢不敦儒素，令學生番直左右，雖有讓侯微善，不得稱無倫輩，嬰為浮華之目。

translations.literal: Hong memorialized Hui did not cultivate Confucian plainness—ordered students rotate duty at side—though had yielding noble slight goodness—cannot be called peerless—Ying gave florid label.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong argued Feng Hui’s stunt disgraced scholarship—Zhai Ying’s praise was mere fashion.

sentences.zh: 遂免嬰官，朝廷憚之。

translations.literal: Thereupon dismissed Ying office—court feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Ying fell—officials dreaded Cui Hong.

sentences.zh: 尋為尚書左丞，時人為之語曰：「叢生棘刺，來自博陵。

translations.literal: Soon minister of the left—men of time made saying: "Thorns in thickets—come from Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon vice minister spawned a rhyme: "Thorns from Boling—

sentences.zh: 在南為鷂，在北為鷹。

translations.literal: In south is goshawk—in north is eagle.
translations.idiomatic: south as goshawk—north as eagle."

sentences.zh: 」選吏部尚書，舉用甄明，門無私謁。

translations.literal: " Selected minister of personnel—promotions clear—gate without private visits.
translations.idiomatic: As minister of personnel he barred private pleading.

sentences.zh: 薦雍州刺史郤詵代己為左丞。

translations.literal: Recommended Yongzhou inspector Xi Shen replace himself as minister of left.
translations.idiomatic: He named Xi Shen of Yongzhou to succeed him as vice minister.

sentences.zh: 詵後糾洪，洪謂人曰：「我舉郤丞而還奏我，是挽弩自射也。

translations.literal: Shen later impeached Hong—Hong told men: "I raised Vice-director Xi yet he memorializes me—this draws crossbow to shoot self.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shen impeached his patron—Cui Hong likened it to shooting oneself.

sentences.zh: 」詵聞曰：「昔趙宣子任韓厥為司馬，以軍法戮宣子之僕。

translations.literal: " Shen hearing said: "Of old Zhao Dun appointed Han Jue as marshal—by military law executed Dun’s groom.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shen cited Zhao Dun and Han Jue—loyal officers punish even patrons’ servants.

sentences.zh: 宣子謂諸大夫曰：'可賀我矣，我選厥也任其事。

translations.literal: Dun told assembled grandees: 'Congratulate me—I chose Jue for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dun rejoiced at Han Jue’s integrity.

sentences.zh: '崔侯為國舉才，我以才見舉，惟官是視，各明至公，何故私言乃至此！

translations.literal: 'Lord Cui raised talent for state—I raised by talent—only office viewed—each illuminates utmost fairness—why private words reach here!
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shen said merit matters—not personal debt.

sentences.zh: 」洪聞其言而重之。

translations.literal: " Hong hearing his words esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong respected the reply.

sentences.zh: 洪口不言貨財，手不執珠玉。

translations.literal: Hong mouth did not speak goods wealth—hand did not hold pearls jade.
translations.idiomatic: He neither hoarded coin nor fingered gems.

sentences.zh: 汝南王亮常晏公卿，以琉璃鐘行酒。

translations.literal: Prince of Runan Liang often banqueted dukes and ministers—used glass bell-cup to pass wine.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang feasted ministers with a glass wine bowl.

sentences.zh: 酒及洪，洪不執。

translations.literal: Wine reached Hong—Hong did not take.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong refused the cup.

sentences.zh: 亮問其故，對曰：「慮有執玉不趨之義故爾」。

translations.literal: Liang asked cause—replied: "Fearing meaning of holding jade not hurry—therefore thus."
translations.idiomatic: He cited ritual modesty—holding jade requires solemn pace.

sentences.zh: 然實乖其常性，故為詭說。

translations.literal: Yet truly violated his constant nature—therefore made crafty explanation.
translations.idiomatic: He invented etiquette to mask stinginess.

sentences.zh: 楊駿誅，洪與都水使者王佑親，坐見黜。

translations.literal: Yang Jun executed—Hong with commissioner of waters Wang You intimate—sat and saw demotion.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Jun fell—his tie to Wang You cost him rank.

sentences.zh: 後為大司農，卒於官。

translations.literal: Later minister of agriculture—died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as minister of agriculture.

translations.literal: Equals sign (scribal section marker in source).
translations.idiomatic: (Section break.)

sentences.zh: 子廓

translations.literal: Son Kuo
translations.idiomatic: His son Cui Kuo

sentences.zh: =子廓，散騎侍郎，亦以正直稱。

translations.literal: =Kuo, attendant at casual riding—also by upright straight praised.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Kuo served as attendant—praised like his father.

sentences.zh: 郭奕

translations.literal: Guo Yi
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi

sentences.zh: 郭奕，字大業，太原陽曲人也。

translations.literal: Guo Yi, courtesy name Daye, native of Yangqu in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi, styled Daye, came from Yangqu in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 少有重名，山濤稱其高簡有雅量。

translations.literal: From youth had heavy fame—Shan Tao praised his lofty spare spacious capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao admired his calm restraint.

sentences.zh: 初為野王令，羊祜常過之，奕歎曰：「羊叔子何必減郭大業！

translations.literal: First magistrate of Yewang—Yang Hu often visited—Yi sighed: "Uncle Yangzi why must diminish Guo Daye!
translations.idiomatic: Hosting Yang Hu he boasted they were peers—then reconsidered.

sentences.zh: 」少選復往，又歎曰：「羊叔子去人遠矣。

translations.literal: " Shortly again went—again sighed: "Uncle Yangzi far surpasses men.
translations.idiomatic: On reflection Yang Hu towered above ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 」遂送祜出界數百里，坐此免官。

translations.literal: " Then escorted Hu beyond boundary several hundred li—sat because dismissed office.
translations.idiomatic: He escorted Yang Hu hundreds of li past his border—lost his post for it.

sentences.zh: 咸熙末，為文帝相國主薄。

translations.literal: Late Xiandi—became Prince Wen’s minister-of-state chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Late Wei he served Prince Zhao’s chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時鍾會反于蜀，荀勖即會之從甥，少長會家，勖為文帝掾，奕啟出之。

translations.literal: At time Zhong Hui rebelled in Shu—Xun Xu was Hui’s nephew—raised from youth in Hui household—Xu was Prince Wen aide—Yi memorialize remove him.
translations.idiomatic: He urged removing Xun Xu—Zhong Hui’s kinsman—from Prince Zhao’s staff during Shu revolt.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不用，然知其雅正。

translations.literal: Emperor though did not use—yet knew his upright correctness.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao noted his integrity despite rejecting the memo.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，初建東宮，以奕及鄭默並為中庶子。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu mounting throne—first established eastern palace—made Yi and Zheng Mo both heir-adjuncts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu named him heir adjunct with Zheng Mo.

sentences.zh: 遷右衛率、驍騎將軍，封平陵男。

translations.literal: Promoted colonel of right guard—general Who Gallops Cavalry—enfeoffed Baron of Pingling.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to guard colonel and cavalry general—Baron of Pingling.

sentences.zh: 咸寧初，遷雍州刺史、鷹揚將軍，尋假赤幢曲蓋、鼓吹。

translations.literal: Early Xianning—promoted inspector of Yongzhou—general Who Raises Hawk—soon borrowed crimson canopy curved parasol—military band.
translations.idiomatic: Early Xianning he governed Yongzhou with general’s banners and band.

sentences.zh: 奕有寡姊，隨奕之官，姊下僮僕多有奸犯，而為人所糾。

translations.literal: Yi had widowed elder sister—followed Yi to office—sister’s servants many wicked offenders—yet impeached by others.
translations.idiomatic: His widowed sister’s servants broke laws—others impeached him.

sentences.zh: 奕省按畢，曰：「大丈夫豈當以老姊求名？

translations.literal: Yi examined finished—said: "Great man how should use old sister seek fame?
translations.idiomatic: He refused to trade on kinship for reputation.

sentences.zh: 」遂遣而不問。

translations.literal: " Then sent away without questioning.
translations.idiomatic: He released the matter—preserving family peace.

sentences.zh: 時亭長李含有俊才，而門寒為豪族所排，奕用為別駕，含後果有名位，時以奕為知人。

translations.literal: At time precinct chief Li Han had splendid talent—yet gate humble pressed by powerful clan—Yi employed as aide—Han afterward indeed won name position—time took Yi as knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted clerk Li Han despite mighty families’ spite—later hailed as a judge of talent.

sentences.zh: 太康中，徵為尚書。

translations.literal: Taikang period—summoned minister of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang recalled him to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 奕有重名，當世朝臣皆出其下。

translations.literal: Yi had heavy fame—contemporary court ministers all below him.
translations.idiomatic: Peers ranked beneath his stature.

sentences.zh: 時帝委任楊駿，奕表駿小器，不可任以社稷。

translations.literal: At time Emperor entrusted Yang Jun—Yi memorialized Jun petty vessel—cannot entrust altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He warned that Yang Jun was too small for state duty.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，駿後果誅。

translations.literal: Emperor did not listen—Jun afterward indeed executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu ignored him—Yang Jun soon died.

sentences.zh: 及奕疾病，詔賜錢二十萬，日給酒米。

translations.literal: When Yi fell ill—edict granted cash two hundred thousand—daily supplied wine grain.
translations.idiomatic: Illness brought imperial stipends of cash and grain.

sentences.zh: 卒，太常上諡為景。

translations.literal: Died—minister of ceremonies upward memorial posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry first proposed “Jing.”

sentences.zh: 有司議以貴賤不同號，諡與景皇同，不可，請諡曰穆。

translations.literal: Responsible offices debated noble humble different titles—posthumous same as Emperor Jing—not permissible—request posthumous Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Court noted “Jing” matched Emperor Jing—requested “Mu” instead.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「諡所以旌德表行，按諡法一德不懈為簡。

translations.literal: Edict said: "Posthumous title thereby banners virtue displays conduct—examining posthumous law one virtue unceasing is Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The throne cited the canon “steady”—Jian.

sentences.zh: 奕忠毅清直，立德不渝。

translations.literal: Yi loyal resolute pure straight—established virtue not altered.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi stayed loyal and lucid to the end.

sentences.zh: 」於是遂賜諡曰簡。

translations.literal: " Thereupon granted posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was canonized “Jian.”

sentences.zh: 侯史光

translations.literal: Houshi Guang
translations.idiomatic: Houshi Guang

sentences.zh: 侯史光，字孝明，東萊掖人也。

translations.literal: Houshi Guang, courtesy name Xiaoming, native of Ye in Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Houshi Guang, styled Xiaoming, came from Ye in Donglai.

sentences.zh: 幼有才悟，受學于同縣劉夏。

translations.literal: From youth had talent perception—received learning from same county Liu Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Liu Xia in his county.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，州辟別駕。

translations.literal: Nominated filial incorrupt—province summoned aide.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended filial and honest—provincial aide.

sentences.zh: 咸熙初，為洛陽典農中郎將，封關中侯。

translations.literal: Early Xianxi—Luoyang agrarian colonel—enfeoffed marquis within Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Early Xianxi he commanded Luoyang farming troops—Marquis Within the Pass.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，拜散騎常侍，尋兼侍中。

translations.literal: Taishi beginning—appointed regular attendant at casual riding—soon concurrently palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi brought him to the attendant corps and palace.

sentences.zh: 與皇甫陶、荀暠持節循省風俗，及還，奏事稱旨，轉城門校尉，進爵臨海侯。

translations.literal: With Huangfu Tao, Xun Gao holding credentials toured inspected customs—when returned—memorialized matters fitting intent—transferred colonel of City Gates—advanced noble rank marquis of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Touring the provinces with Huangfu Tao he earned promotion to colonel of the gates—Marquis of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 其年詔曰：「光忠亮篤素，有居正執義之心，歷職內外，恪勤在公，其以光為御史中丞。

translations.literal: That year edict said: "Guang loyal bright devoted plain—has dwell upright hold righteousness heart—served inner outer offices—scrupulous diligent in public—make Guang palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised his integrity—named him imperial secretary.

sentences.zh: 雖屈其列校之位，亦所以伸其司直之才。

translations.literal: Though bent his ranked-colonel position—also thereby extend his straightening talent.
translations.idiomatic: The sideways move showcased his censorial grit.

sentences.zh: 」光在職寬而不縱。

translations.literal: " Guang in office lenient yet not lax.
translations.idiomatic: As secretary he was firm but fair.

sentences.zh: 太保王祥久疾廢朝，光奏請免之，詔優祥而寢光奏。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Wang Xiang long ill ceased court—Guang memorialized request dismiss—edict favored Xiang yet shelved Guang memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He urged retiring Wang Xiang—the emperor honored Wang Xiang and ignored the memo.

sentences.zh: 後遷少府，卒官，詔賜朝服一具、衣一襲、錢三十萬、布百匹。

translations.literal: Later promoted minister of the privy purse—died in office—edict gifted court robes one set—garments one suit—cash thirty thousand—cloth one hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted privy-treasury minister, he died in office; the court sent burial robes, thirty thousand cash, and a hundred bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 及葬，又詔曰：「光厲志守約，有清忠之節。

translations.literal: When buried—again edict said: "Guang hardened will kept restraint—had pure loyal bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His obsequies brought praise for austerity and loyalty.

sentences.zh: 家極貧儉，其賜錢五十萬。

translations.literal: House extremely poor frugal—grant cash fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The throne added fifty thousand cash for his destitute household.

sentences.zh: 」光儒學博古，歷官著績，文筆奏議皆有條理。

translations.literal: " Guang Confucian learning broad antiquity—each office showed merit—literary brush memorials all had order.
translations.idiomatic: Houshi Guang mastered classical lore; his memorials were models of clarity.

sentences.zh: 長子玄嗣，官至玄菟太守。

translations.literal: Eldest son Xuan succeeded—office reached prefect of Xuantu.
translations.idiomatic: Son Houshi Xuan rose to Xuantu prefect.

sentences.zh: 卒，子施嗣，東莞太守。

translations.literal: Died—son Shi succeeded—prefect of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: He died; son Houshi Shi became Dongguan prefect.

sentences.zh: 何攀

translations.literal: He Pan
translations.idiomatic: He Pan

sentences.zh: 何攀，字惠興，蜀郡郫人也。

translations.literal: He Pan, courtesy name Huixing, native of Pi in Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He Pan, styled Huixing, came from Pi in Shu.

sentences.zh: 仕州為主薄。

translations.literal: Served province as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 屬刺史皇甫晏為牙門張弘所害，誣以大逆。

translations.literal: When Inspector Huangfu Yan was harmed by camp gate Zhang Hong—slandered with great treason.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Huangfu Yan was murdered by Zhang Hong and smeared as a traitor.

sentences.zh: 時攀適丁母喪，遂詣梁州拜表，證晏不反，故晏冤理得申。

translations.literal: At time Pan happened mourning mother—thereupon went to Liangzhou submitting memorial—proved Yan did not rebel—therefore Yan’s wrong managed to clear.
translations.idiomatic: Though mourning his mother, he rode to Liangzhou and cleared Huangfu Yan’s name.

sentences.zh: 王濬為益州，辟為別駕。

translations.literal: Wang Jun as Yi province—summoned as aide.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun made him provincial aide in Yi.

sentences.zh: 濬謀伐吳，遣攀奉表詣台，口陳事機，詔再引見，乃令張華與攀籌量進時討之宜。

translations.literal: Jun schemed attacking Wu—sent Pan bearing memorial to court—orally stated opportunity—edict twice summoned audience—ordered Zhang Hua with Pan deliberate advancing timing of attack fitness.
translations.idiomatic: He Pan carried Wang Jun’s Wu campaign memorial to Luoyang and planned timing with Zhang Hua.

sentences.zh: 濬兼遣攀過羊祜，面陳伐吳之策。

translations.literal: Jun also sent Pan visit Yang Hu—face to face state attacking Wu strategies.
translations.idiomatic: He also briefed Yang Hu in person on the Wu invasion.

sentences.zh: 攀善於將命，帝善之，詔攀參濬軍事。

translations.literal: Pan good at carrying orders—Emperor praised—ordered Pan assist Jun military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His diplomacy pleased Emperor Wu, who attached him to Wang Jun’s staff.

sentences.zh: 及孫皓降于濬，而王渾恚於後機，欲攻濬，攀勸濬送皓與渾，由是事解。

translations.literal: When Sun Hao surrendered to Jun—yet Wang Hun angry at late timing—wished attack Jun—Pan urged Jun deliver Hao to Hun—thereby matter resolved.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Hun nearly attacked Wang Jun over Sun Hao’s surrender, He Pan urged handing the captive to Hun to prevent civil bloodshed.

sentences.zh: 以攀為濬輔國司馬，封關內侯。

translations.literal: Made Pan Jun aids-state marshal—enfeoffed marquis within Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun named him auxiliary marshal—Marquis Within the Pass.

sentences.zh: 轉滎陽令，上便宜十事，甚得名稱。

translations.literal: Transferred Xingyang magistrate—submitted convenient matters ten items—greatly earned reputation.
translations.idiomatic: As Xingyang magistrate he offered ten reform memos and won fame.

sentences.zh: 除廷尉平。

translations.literal: Appointed commandant-ping of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He became a justice assessor.

sentences.zh: 時廷尉卿諸葛沖以攀蜀士，輕之，及共斷疑獄，沖始嘆服。

translations.literal: At time commandant of justice Zhuge Chong because Pan Shu gentleman—slighted him—when together judged doubtful lawsuits—Chong then sighed admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Chong sneered at his Shu origins until joint trials proved his genius.

sentences.zh: 遷宣城太守，不行，轉散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Promoted prefect of Xuancheng—did not go—transferred regular attendant at casual riding.
translations.idiomatic: He declined Xuancheng but joined the attendant corps.

sentences.zh: 楊駿執政，多樹親屬，大開封嘗，欲以恩澤自衛。

translations.literal: Yang Jun holding power—planted many kin—greatly opened investitures rewards—wished by grace shield self.
translations.idiomatic: Regent Yang Jun stuffed offices with kin and blanketed them with patents.

sentences.zh: 攀以為非，乃與石崇共立議奏之。

translations.literal: Pan thought not right—thereupon with Shi Chong jointly stood memorial submitting.
translations.idiomatic: He Pan and Shi Chong jointly condemned the policy.

sentences.zh: 語在崇傳。

translations.literal: Language is in Chong biography.
translations.idiomatic: (See the biography of Shi Chong.)

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: Emperor did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored them.

sentences.zh: 以豫誅駿功，封西城侯，邑萬戶，賜絹萬匹，弟逢平卿侯，兄子逵關中侯。

translations.literal: By merit participating executing Jun—enfeoffed marquis of Xicheng—ten thousand households—gift silk ten thousand bolts—younger brother Feng Pingqing marquis—elder brother’s son Kui marquis within Guan.
translations.idiomatic: For helping purge Yang Jun he gained a ten-thousand-household marquisate—rich bounty—and titles for kin.

sentences.zh: 攀固讓所封戶及絹之半，餘所受者分給中外宗親，略不入己。

translations.literal: Pan firmly declined half of granted households and silk—remainder received distributed inside outside kin—almost none entered self.
translations.idiomatic: He refused half the silk and fiefs—sharing the rest with kin—keeping nothing.

sentences.zh: 遷翊軍校尉，頃之，出為東羌校尉。

translations.literal: Promoted colonel Who Aids Army—shortly—went out colonel of Eastern Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: He became aide colonel then Eastern Qiang colonel.

sentences.zh: 徵為揚州刺史，在任三年，遷大司農。

translations.literal: Summoned inspector of Yang province—in office three years—promoted minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: After three years as Yangzhou inspector he headed the ministry of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 轉兗州刺史，加鷹揚將軍，固讓不就。

translations.literal: Transferred inspector of Yanzhou—added general Who Raises Hawk—firmly declined did not take.
translations.idiomatic: He refused Yanzhou despite general’s banners.

sentences.zh: 太常成粲、左將軍卞粹勸攀蒞職，中詔又加切厲，攀竟稱疾不起。

translations.literal: Minister of ceremonies Cheng Can—general left Bian Cui urged Pan take office—inner edict again stern—Pan ultimately claimed illness did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Court pressure failed—He Pan pleaded sickness.

sentences.zh: 及趙王倫篡位，遣使召攀，更稱疾篤。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun usurped—sent envoy summon Pan—again claimed grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lun’s summons met another refusal—grave illness.

sentences.zh: 倫怒，將誅之，攀不得已，扶疾赴召。

translations.literal: Lun angry—would execute—Pan had no choice—supported illness answered summons.
translations.idiomatic: Lun threatened death—He Pan dragged himself to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 卒于洛陽，時年五十八。

translations.literal: Died in Luoyang—age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died there at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 攀居心平允，蒞官整肅，愛樂人物，敦儒貴才。

translations.literal: Pan dwelling mind fair—holding office stern—loved delighted men—esteemed Confucian prized talent.
translations.idiomatic: Fair-minded and orderly in office, he honored scholars and talent.

sentences.zh: 為梁、益二州中正，引致遺滯。

translations.literal: As grand rectifier for Liang and Yi provinces—drew in stranded men.
translations.idiomatic: As Liang-Yi rectifier he recalled unjustly blocked men.

sentences.zh: 巴西陳壽、閻乂、犍為費立皆西州名士，並被鄉閭所謗，清議十餘年。

translations.literal: Baixi Chen Shou—Yan Yi—Fei Li of Qianwei—all western province famed gentlemen—together slandered by villages—pure discussion over ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou and western scholars suffered decade-long village boycotts.

sentences.zh: 攀申明曲直，咸免冤濫。

translations.literal: Pan clarified crooked straight—all spared wrongful overflow.
translations.idiomatic: He Pan reversed their verdicts—clearing injustice.

sentences.zh: 攀雖居顯職，家甚貧素，無妾媵伎樂，惟以周窮濟乏為事。

translations.literal: Pan though occupied eminent office—house very poor plain—no concubines singing girls—only took relieving poverty aiding want as task.
translations.idiomatic: Despite high rank he stayed poor—no concubines or musicians—only charity.

sentences.zh: 子璋嗣，亦有父風。

translations.literal: Son Zhang succeeded—also had father manner.
translations.idiomatic: Son He Zhang inherited his integrity.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historians’ appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Historians’ appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：幽厲不君，上德猶懷進善；

translations.literal: Historians say: You and Li did not lord—high virtue still cherished advancing goodness;
translations.idiomatic: Even under tyrants worthies still hoped to counsel virtue;

sentences.zh: 共驩在位，大聖之所不堪。

translations.literal: Gong Huan on throne—great sage cannot endure.
translations.idiomatic: petty rulers like Gong Huan exhaust even sages;

sentences.zh: 況乎志士仁人，甯求苟合！

translations.literal: How much more intent gentlemen and benevolent men—would they seek careless conformity!
translations.idiomatic: how much less would principled men trim truth for favor!

sentences.zh: 懷其寵秩，所以系其存亡者也。

translations.literal: Cherishing their favor and salary—thereby ties their survival.
translations.idiomatic: Rank and stipend bind ministers’ survival—

sentences.zh: 雖復自口銷金，投光撫劍，馳書北闕，敗車猶踐，而諫主不易，譏臣實難。

translations.literal: Though again mouths melt metal—cast aside brilliance grasp sword—gallop memorial northern gate—broken cart still tread—yet remonstrating lord not easy—mocking ministers truly hard.
translations.idiomatic: yet even facing ruin remonstrating proves harder than flattering—truth cuts both ways.

sentences.zh: 劉毅一遇寬容，任和兩遭膚受，詳觀餘烈，亦各其心焉。

translations.literal: Liu Yi once met tolerance—Ren and He twice suffered shallow belief—closely observing remaining deeds—each also their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi won rare patience—Ren Kai and He Jiao suffered credulous courts—each followed conscience nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 若夫武陔懷魏臣之志，崔洪愛郤詵之道，長升勸王彌之尊，何攀從趙倫之命，君子之人，觀乎臨事者也。

translations.literal: As for Wu Gai cherishing Wei minister resolve—Cui Hong loving Xi Shen’s way—Changsheng urging Wang Mi’s honor—He Pan obeying Zhao Lun’s order—gentleman quality—observe them at crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Gai kept Wei loyalty; Cui Hong praised Xi Shen; Liu Tun courted Wang Mi; He Pan answered Prince Lun—character shows in crisis.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：仲雄初令，忠謇揚庭。

translations.literal: Praise says: Zhongxiong first command—loyal blunt raised court.
translations.idiomatic: Verse: Liu Yi’s early zeal shook the court—

sentences.zh: 身方諸葛，帝擬桓、靈。

translations.literal: Body compared Zhuge—Emperor likened Huan Ling.
translations.idiomatic: likened to stern ministers—yet matched with doomed Han emperors;

sentences.zh: 大業非楊，元褒誚賈。

translations.literal: Great enterprise not Yang—Yuanbao mocked Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Daye refused Yang Jun’s tide—Ren Kai mocked Jia Chong;

sentences.zh: 和氏條暢，堪施大廈。

translations.literal: He clan lithe—fit to roof great hall.
translations.idiomatic: He Jiao stood tall as ridge timber;

sentences.zh: 崔門不謁，聲飛朝野。

translations.literal: Cui gate unvisited—voice flies court wild.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong barred favor-seekers yet fame soared;

sentences.zh: 侯史、武陔，輔佐之才。

translations.literal: Houshi and Wu Gai—aiding talents.
translations.idiomatic: Houshi Guang and Wu Gai served as fine assistants;

sentences.zh: 何攀平允，冤濫多回。

translations.literal: He Pan fair—wrongful overflow much turned.
translations.idiomatic: He Pan’s fairness redeemed many wrongs.
